## 1. Satisfactory — ficsit.app / SMR ✅ CONFIRMED, best-in-class for a host

**Endpoint:** `https://api.ficsit.app/v2/query` — GraphQL, **POST**, **no auth**, no API key. Live-verified 200. `/v1/` returns 404 (v1 survives only as the download path). Introspection is **fully open** (93 types) — `{"query":"{ __schema { types { name fields { name } } } }"}`.

Live: `getMods(filter:{limit:N})` → `count: 1567`. Also `getModByReference(modReference:"RefinedPower")`.

**Mod fields (introspected, exact):** `id, name, short_description, full_description, logo, logo_thumbhash, source_url, creator_id, approved, views, downloads, hotness, popularity, updated_at, created_at, last_version_date, mod_reference, hidden, tags, compatibility, network_use_disclosure, ai_use_disclosure, toggle_explicit_content, authors, version, versions, latestVersions`.

> **There is NO `license` field.** I introspected every field of all 93 types for `licen|legal|copyright|terms` — **zero hits**. Best proxy is `source_url` (often a GitHub repo → then use the GitHub license API, item 9).

Nice extras: `logo` is a ready CDN webp (`https://storage.ficsit.app/file/smr-prod-s3/images/mods/{id}/logo.webp`), `logo_thumbhash` gives you free blur-up placeholders, and `compatibility { EA { state note } EXP { state note } }` gives per-branch compat.

**Version fields:** `id, mod_id, version, sml_version, game_version, required_on_remote, changelog, downloads, stability, approved, link, targets, metadata, size, hash, dependencies, virustotal_results`.

**The two killer fields for a hosting company:**
- `required_on_remote: true/false` — tells you outright whether the mod must go on the server.
- `targets[] { targetName, link, size, hash }` where `targetName ∈ {Windows, WindowsServer, LinuxServer}`. **You download the LinuxServer build directly** — a fraction of the client size (40MB vs 237MB for Refined Power).

**Download — live-verified end to end, unauthenticated:**
```
GET https://api.ficsit.app/v1/version/{versionId}/{target}/download
→ 302 → https://storage.ficsit.app/file/smr-prod-s3/mods/{modId}/{Name}-{target}-{ver}.smod
→ 200, 40,384,686 bytes
```
SHA256 of the downloaded file matched the API's `hash` field **exactly** (`664153ba4c20…`). `.smod` is a plain zip. Backblaze B2 behind Cloudflare, `cache-control: max-age=1800`.

**Rate limits:** none documented, none exposed — no `x-ratelimit-*` or `retry-after` headers on repeated bursts. Envoy + Cloudflare fronted, so assume undocumented protection exists. Be polite.

**Dedicated server install (this is the part that matters):** SML 3.7.0+ added server-side support. Per the [official dedicated server docs](https://docs.ficsit.app/satisfactory-modding/latest/ForUsers/DedicatedServerSetup.html): *"client players must have the same mods installed as the server to be able to join."* Two supported tools — SMM (GUI) and **[ficsit-cli](https://github.com/satisfactorymodding/ficsit-cli)**, which *"can be installed locally or directly on the server itself"* — that's your install path. Both connect over **SFTP (recommended, port 22), FTP (21), SMB/CIFS (445), or a local path**, pointed at the directory containing `FactoryServer.sh`. Mods must be *"specially compiled and packaged"* per server type — hence the `targets` field. **The server must be shut down before installing or updating**, as a running server locks files. ficsit-cli ships Debian/Fedora/Alpine packages and linux amd64/arm64 binaries.

Practical architecture: you don't need ficsit-cli at all. Query GraphQL → pick the `LinuxServer` target → download → verify `hash` → unzip into the server's mods dir. But ficsit-cli handles dependency resolution, which the raw API makes you do yourself via `versions.dependencies`.

**⚠️ ToS — the one real problem.** `https://ficsit.app/tos` is a client-rendered SPA (curl returns nothing) and the `forums.ficsit.app/tos.html` mirror was 503 throughout, so **I could not retrieve the verbatim text** — the following are search-engine-surfaced quotes I could not independently confirm against the live page, and you should have someone open it in a browser before shipping:

> "All user-submitted content is provided for personal use. You are not entitled to redistribute, repackage, sell, or otherwise distribute content without express permission from the associated content owner(s)"

> "any user-submitted content may not contain links to off-site mod binaries or archives"

If accurate, that clause is aimed at reuploading, but a host that **caches** `.smod` files and serves them to paying customers is arguably "redistributing." **Recommendation: proxy-and-stream from `storage.ficsit.app` at install time rather than building your own mirror, and keep attribution + a link back to the mod page.** Combined with the total absence of license metadata, Satisfactory is a "hot-link, don't mirror" source.

## 2. Vintage Story — mods.vintagestory.at ✅ CONFIRMED, official and documented

**Base:** `https://mods.vintagestory.at/api/` — plain GET, JSON, **no auth**. Officially documented at [github.com/anegostudios/vsmoddb](https://github.com/anegostudios/vsmoddb) (the site footer links to it as "Json Api"). Every endpoint below live-tested 200.

| Endpoint | Result |
|---|---|
| `/api/mods` | 200, 3.78 MB, **8,600 mods** (site footer claims 9,994 total) |
| `/api/mod/{modid}` | 200 — accepts **numeric id (11868) or urlalias string** ("pmaccess") |
| `/api/authors` | 200, 4.19 MB, `{userid, name}` |
| `/api/gameversions` | 200, `{tagid, name, color}` |
| `/api/tags` | 200, `{tagid, name, color}` |
| `/api/comments/{assetid}` | 200 |

**List fields:** `modid, assetid, downloads, follows, trendingpoints, comments, name, summary, modidstrs[], author, urlalias, side, type, logo, tags[], lastreleased`.

**Detail fields:** adds `text` (full HTML description), `logofilename, logofile, logofiledb, homepageurl, sourcecodeurl, trailervideourl, issuetrackerurl, wikiurl, created, lastmodified, screenshots[]`, and `releases[]`.

**Release fields:** `releaseid, mainfile, filename, fileid, downloads, tags[] (game versions), modidstr, modversion, created, changelog`.

> **No license field.** Confirmed by dumping the complete key set of a detail response — there is no `license` key anywhere. `sourcecodeurl` is your proxy.

Two fields are directly load-bearing for a host: **`side`** (`"both" | "server" | "client"`) and **`type`** (`"mod"` / `"theme"` / etc.). `side` is exactly the server-side filter you want, and it's free.

**Downloads — three working forms, all live-verified unauthenticated:**
```
https://mods.vintagestory.at/download?fileid=123360          → 200 (legacy, works)
https://mods.vintagestory.at/download/123360/{filename}.zip  → 200 (current)
https://moddbcdn.vintagestory.at/{hashed}.zip?dl={filename}  → 200 (direct CDN, from `mainfile`)
```
All three land on the same `moddbcdn.vintagestory.at` object.

**Bonus — an undocumented-in-practice v2 API built for exactly your use case.** I cracked the parameter format by probing:
```
GET /api/v2/mods/install-information?ids=<modidstr>@<version>
→ {"data":{"playermodelaccess":{"fileName":"…zip","fileUrl":"/download/123360/…zip"}}}
```
Batchable via comma/repeat, **GET only** (POST returns 405 with an explicit "Try again using GET"). Requires the **string** modid — numeric id returns `errorCode 4041`; a wildcard version returns `4001`. Also live: `/api/v2/mods/{modid}/releases/latest` returning `{releaseId, identifier, version, compatibleGameVersions[], created, fileName, fileUrl}`. This is the endpoint the launcher/server-updater ecosystem uses — use it for update checks instead of re-pulling mod detail.

**Rate limits:** none documented, none exposed. `/api/mods` is a 3.8 MB full dump — cache it, don't poll it.

**ToS — [mods.vintagestory.at/terms](https://mods.vintagestory.at/terms), retrieved verbatim.** This one is *favourable*:

> "Anego Studios may display, publish and distribute the code, assets and other materials that comprise your mod, free of charge, to any mod user, and that any mod user may install and use your mod free of charge. This license will continue indefinitely unless terminated by agreement."

> "**Mod User:** A visitor of this site that downloads your mod **or a player that downloads your mod through the game client**."

> "Any license terms contained in the mod itself must be compatible with the terms put forth by Anego Studios."

And the redistribution warning:

> "For reuploads of a mod, modified or not, make sure that in addition to the terms put forth by Anego Studios this action complies with the original mod's license."

> "Note that **no license does not imply public domain, but that all rights are reserved.** Most importantly this means that you are not allowed to reupload, modified or not, any such mods without explicit approval from the original author."

Reading: fetching on a customer's behalf is fine (they're a "mod user"). **Standing up your own mirror is a "reupload" and is not.** Same conclusion as Satisfactory — stream, don't mirror. Note the ToS is silent on API/scraping entirely, and the API is officially published, so indexing metadata is clearly fine.

## 3. Terraria / tModLoader ❌ No usable API — Steam Workshop only

**The legacy `javid.ddns.net` API is a fossil. I proved it live.** All four PHP endpoints return HTTP 200, which looks promising and is misleading:

- `listmods.php` returns real XML — but **27 mods total, newest `updateTimeStamp` 2016-02-11**, fields `displayname, name, version, author, description, download, downloads, updateTimeStamp`.
- The advertised download format `download.php?Down=mods/{Name}.tmod` returns **404** (36-byte error body).
- Server is `lighttpd/1.4.53`, root last modified **2020-11-18**.

Do not build against it. Mods now live on **Steam Workshop app `1281930`** (tModLoader is its own Steam app, separate from Terraria's `105600`). The in-game "Mod Browser" is a front-end onto Steam Workshop.

**Dedicated server install — from the [official DedicatedServerUtils README](https://github.com/tModLoader/tModLoader/blob/stable/patches/tModLoader/Terraria/release_extras/DedicatedServerUtils/README.md) plus the actual script source, which I read:**

> "The steam workshop does not use mod names to identify mods, so a modpack should be made to install mods from the workshop."

Flow: on a *client*, Workshop → Mod Packs → "Save Enabled as New Mod Pack" → "Open Mod Pack Folder" → produces **`install.txt`** (workshop IDs, one per line) and **`enabled.json`** (internal mod names to activate). Both go into a `Mods` subdirectory on the server, then `./manage-tModLoaderServer.sh install-mods`.

> "No mods will be installed if `install.txt` is missing, and no mods will be enabled if `enabled.json` is missing."

From `manage-tModLoaderServer.sh` source (the part the README doesn't document):
```bash
# one +workshop_download_item per line of install.txt
steamcmd_command="$steamcmd_command +workshop_download_item 1281930 $line"
eval "'$steam_cmd' +force_install_dir '$folder' +login anonymous$steamcmd_command +quit"
# server launch:
./LaunchUtils/ScriptCaller.sh -server -config "$folder/serverconfig.txt" \
  -steamworkshopfolder "$folder/steamapps/workshop" -tmlsavedirectory "$folder"
```
**`+login anonymous` works** — no Steam account needed. `-steamworkshopfolder` and `-tmlsavedirectory` are the two flags your panel needs. It also uses `+app_update 1281930` to install the server itself.

**Catalog implication:** your only metadata source is the Steam Workshop APIs (covered in whoever's researching Steam Workshop). You can generate `install.txt`/`enabled.json` yourself rather than making customers build a modpack on a desktop client — that's a real UX win, but you need the internal mod name for `enabled.json`, which is inside the `.tmod` file, not in Workshop metadata. Plan to read it post-download.

## 4. Valheim ✅ Thunderstore + BepInEx confirmed dominant

Thunderstore is the catalog (researched separately); BepInEx is the loader. Canonical pack: **`denikson/BepInExPack_Valheim`** on Thunderstore.

**Server install:** extract the pack at the server root, giving `BepInEx/`, `doorstop_libs/`, `unstripped_corlib/`, `doorstop_config.ini`, and **`start_server_bepinex.sh`** — you launch that script instead of `start_server.sh`. On Linux the doorstop injects via `LD_PRELOAD`/`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` pointing at `doorstop_libs` (on Windows it's the `winhttp.dll` proxy DLL). Mods are DLLs dropped in **`BepInEx/plugins/`**.

**Server-side vs client-side:** there is no machine-readable flag. Thunderstore package *categories* include "Server-side"/"Client-side" tags that authors self-apply — usable but unreliable. Most Valheim mods require **matching versions on both server and client**; a mismatch surfaces as a version-check disconnect rather than a crash. Practical advice: surface the author's tag, and warn customers that clients likely need the same mod+version.

**Nexus presence:** minimal and legacy. Thunderstore won decisively. Don't invest in Nexus for Valheim.

## 5. Palworld ⚠️ The "barely" premise is now OUT OF DATE

This is the finding most likely to change your plan. Palworld now has **official, first-party Steam Workshop mod support with an explicit server-side contract**, documented by Pocketpair at [docs.palworldgame.com/settings-and-operation/mod/](https://docs.palworldgame.com/settings-and-operation/mod/).

Live-verified: `https://steamcommunity.com/app/1623730/workshop/` returns 200, and the browse page yields **30 workshop item IDs in the 3.80-billion range** (i.e. recently published, active).

**Official install rules — deployment targets by mod type:**

| Type | Destination |
|---|---|
| UE4SS | `Mods\NativeMods\UE4SS` |
| Lua | `Mods\NativeMods\UE4SS\Mods\{PackageName}` |
| PalSchema | `Mods\NativeMods\UE4SS\Mods\PalSchema\mods\{PackageName}` |
| LogicMods | `Pal\Content\Paks\LogicMods` |
| Paks | `Pal\Content\Paks\~WorkshopMods\{PackageName}` |

The server reads from **`Mods/Workshop`, in the same directory as the server executable**, or an explicitly configured Workshop directory. Default Steam path is `steamapps\workshop\content\1623730`.

**The server-compat flag you need:** every mod ships an `Info.json` with a `PackageName` and an `InstallRule` section. Per the official docs:

> "if the `InstallRule` section in `Info.json` does **not** include `"IsServer": true`, the mod is not designed to run on servers."

That's a real, first-party, machine-readable server-side filter — better than Valheim or 7D2D have. You can't read it from Workshop metadata though; you must download and inspect `Info.json`.

**The Linux catch, and it's a big one for a host.** UE4SS is **Windows-only**: *"Linux is not officially supported by UE4SS currently which means you will have to utilize Wine or Proton to run your server under Windows."* Install is the `ue4ss` folder + `dwmapi.dll` into `Win64`. So on a Linux fleet:
- **`.pak` mods → work on both Linux and Windows servers.**
- **`PalSchema`** (JSON-based data tweaks — drop rates, breeding times, capture multipliers, item stats) **works on both** and needs no UE4SS.
- **UE4SS / Lua mods → Windows only.** Wine/Proton otherwise.

If your Palworld fleet is Linux, scope the catalog to `.pak` + PalSchema and say so plainly in the UI. Also note the modding wiki warns that host-provided auto-UE4SS installers are a common failure source (outdated versions) — if you build one, version it carefully.

**Nexus Mods** carries Palworld mods too, but Workshop is now the officially supported path. Prefer Workshop.

## 6. 7 Days to Die ⚠️ Nexus for catalog; launcher XML is legacy

**No mod API.** Nexus Mods is the main source (covered separately).

**The 7D2D Mod Launcher** ([SphereII/The7D2DModLauncher](https://github.com/SphereII/The7D2DModLauncher)) does have a machine-readable catalog, and I fetched it live — but it's **a federated set of hand-maintained XML files, not an API**. `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SphereII/7D2DConfig/master/7Days2Mod.xml` (7,773 bytes) plus ~25 sibling XMLs in the same repo (`Default.xml`, `Haidrgna.xml` 30 KB, `Valmar.xml`, `TheFunPimps.xml`, `Tin.xml`, `SDX.xml`, …). Schema:

```xml
<Servers><ServerGroup Name Logo Description>
  <Server Name Logo>
    <Description/><RSS/><ReleaseNotes/>
    <Downloads><Download>https://github.com/.../archive/master.zip</Download></Downloads>
  </Server>
</ServerGroup></Servers>
```

So it's essentially **a curated index of GitHub zip URLs** — usable for big overhauls (Darkness Falls, Undead Legacy, War of the Walkers) but there's no version, no license, no game-version compat field, and no icon beyond a banner URL. Treat it as a seed list, not a catalog.

**Server install:** upload the extracted mod folder (containing `ModInfo.xml`) into `/Mods/` on the server, and **set `EACEnabled=false` in `serverconfig.xml`.** EAC-enabled clients cannot connect to EAC-disabled servers and vice versa — server and all players must match. Most overhauls also need a fresh world. Every client needs matching mod files. The Mod Launcher disables EAC automatically when launching a modpack profile.

For a host: the EAC toggle is the thing to automate and to warn about loudly — it's the #1 support ticket generator here.

## 7. Project Zomboid ✅ Steam Workshop only — and the app-ID trap

Steam Workshop is the only meaningful source. No non-Workshop distribution of note, no API.

**Server install — two separate `servertest.ini` keys, and you need both:**
```ini
WorkshopItems=624489512;972954692
Mods=CraftableAxes;Katana
```
- `WorkshopItems=` takes **numeric Steam Workshop IDs** (from the Workshop URL). This controls *download*.
- `Mods=` takes **internal text mod IDs** baked inside each mod — not display names. This controls *activation*.
- Semicolon-separated, **no spaces**.
- Fill only `WorkshopItems` → files land on disk but never load. Fill only `Mods` → the game tries to activate something never downloaded.

**⚠️ The app-ID trap:** `steamcmd +login anonymous +workshop_download_item 108600 {id}` — **108600 is the PZ *client* app ID**, not the dedicated server app (380870). Using the server app ID here fails. Worth hard-coding correctly.

**Catalog implication:** the internal mod ID for `Mods=` lives in the downloaded mod's `mod.info` file, not in Workshop metadata — same pattern as tModLoader. Your installer must download first, then parse, then write the ini. A mod can also contain *multiple* mod IDs, so parse all of them. Map files are a third key (`Map=`) if you support those.

## 8. ARK: Survival Ascended ✅ CONFIRMED — CurseForge, not Steam Workshop

Confirmed from both the partnership announcement and server-admin docs.

- **ASE (Survival Evolved)** = Steam Workshop. *"The original ARK: Survival Evolved was powered by Steam Workshop, with mod authors publishing over 10,000 mods."*
- **ASA (Survival Ascended)** = **CurseForge exclusively**, via a Studio Wildcard × CurseForge (Overwolf) partnership, driven by console cross-platform support: *"For the first time ever, ARK mods crafted on PC will be able to run on consoles."* "Cloud Cooking" means modders publish once from the devkit and CurseForge builds per-platform. Dedicated ASA portal: `https://arksa.curseforge.com/`.

**Dedicated server install — exact launch args:**

```
-mods=<ModId1>[,<ModId2>[...]]
```
> "CurseForge Mod Project IDs. **Mods are updated automatically when starting the server.**"

```
-passivemods=<ModId1>[,<ModId2>[...]]
```
> "This option disables a mod's functionality while still loading its data. This is useful if, for example, you want to have S-Dinos on Astraeos… while preventing them from spawning on The Island."

**Critically: `-automanagedmods` and `-MapModID` are OBSOLETE for ASA.** They were the *ASE/Steam* mechanism (`-automanagedmods` = *"Steam only, automatic MOD download/installation/updating. Mod IDs are listed in Game.ini under `[ModInstaller]`"*), along with the deprecated `?GameModIds=`. If your panel has an ASE-era `-automanagedmods` toggle, it's wrong for ASA.

**This is the easiest integration in the whole list.** The server downloads and updates mods itself from CurseForge — you never touch a file. Your job reduces to: let the customer pick CurseForge project IDs, write them into `-mods=`, restart. All you need from the CurseForge API is metadata for the picker (game ID 83374 for ASA), which is the separately-researched CurseForge workstream. Note the ASA mod content on CurseForge sits under Wildcard-specific [moderation guidelines](https://support.curseforge.com/support/solutions/articles/9000232898-moderation-guidelines-for-ark-survival-ascended).

## 9. GitHub Releases ✅ All claims verified live — and the only real license source

**REST API:** `https://api.github.com`

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/releases` | all releases (paginated) |
| `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/releases/latest` | latest non-prerelease, non-draft |
| `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/releases/tags/{tag}` | by tag |
| `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/license` | **license with SPDX id** |
| `GET /licenses` | license list |

**Live test, `EssentialsX/Essentials/releases/latest`:** tag `2.22.0`, published `2026-05-31`, assets with `name, size, content_type, download_count, browser_download_url, url`.

**Asset download — live-verified unauthenticated, but note the redirect:**
```
https://github.com/EssentialsX/Essentials/releases/download/2.22.0/EssentialsX-2.22.0.jar
→ 200, 4,861,125 bytes, valid JAR
```
**⚠️ It redirects to a SIGNED, EXPIRING URL** on `release-assets.githubusercontent.com` — I observed `se=2026-09-19T03:49:55Z`, roughly a **1-hour** expiry, with an SAS signature and a JWT. So: **`browser_download_url` is stable and cacheable; the resolved final URL is not.** Never persist the resolved URL. (The alternative is the asset `url` with `Accept: application/octet-stream`, which needs auth for private repos.)

**LICENSES API — ✅ confirms `spdx_id`, live:**
```json
"license": {
  "key": "gpl-3.0",
  "name": "GNU General Public License v3.0",
  "spdx_id": "GPL-3.0",
  "url": "https://api.github.com/licenses/gpl-3.0",
  "node_id": "MDc6TGljZW5zZTk="
}
```
Also returns the license file `path`, `download_url`, and full base64 `content`. **⚠️ `GET /licenses` returns only 13 licenses** — the *featured* set (agpl-3.0, apache-2.0, bsd-2-clause, bsd-3-clause, bsl-1.0, cc0-1.0, …). Pass `?featured=false` for the full list. Also: GitHub's detection is heuristic — a modified or dual license often returns `"spdx_id": "NOASSERTION"`. Treat that as "unknown, show the file," not as permissive.

**Rate limits — verified live, with one correction to your premise:**
- **Unauthenticated: 60/hr.** I confirmed this the hard way — I exhausted it mid-research. `/rate_limit` returned `{"limit":60,"remaining":0,"used":60}` with `x-ratelimit-limit: 60`, `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, `x-ratelimit-reset`. ✅
- **PAT / authenticated user: 5,000/hr.** ✅
- **GitHub App installation: 5,000/hr base.** *"Installations that are on an organization that have more than 20 users receive another 50 requests per hour for each user"*, **capped at 12,500** — not 15,000.
- **⚠️ The 15,000 figure is Enterprise Cloud only**, not "GitHub Apps on an org": *"If the installation is on a GitHub Enterprise Cloud organization, the installation has a rate limit of 15,000 requests per hour."* Same for OAuth apps and `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Your premise conflated these — **budget for 5,000/hr**, or 12,500 at best.
- `GITHUB_TOKEN` in Actions: 1,000/hr per repository.
- **Release asset *downloads* do not consume the REST rate limit** (they're on a different host), but are subject to abuse detection.

**ToS — [GitHub ToS](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service), retrieved verbatim:**

§H API Terms:
> "Abuse or excessively frequent requests to GitHub via the API may result in the temporary or permanent suspension of your Account's access to the API."

Plus: no sharing tokens to circumvent rate limits, and no using the API to download user data for commercial purposes like recruitment or sales (aimed at scraping *people*, not releases).

§D.5 License Grant to Other Users — **this is the one that governs you**:
> "By making a repository public, you grant other Users a nonexclusive, worldwide license to use, display, perform and reproduce (by forking) Your Content through the Service as permitted by GitHub's functionality. **You may grant additional rights by adopting a license.**"

§D.6:
> "Whenever you add Content to a repository containing notice of a license, you license that Content under the same terms… commonly referred to by the shorthand 'inbound=outbound'."

**Read this carefully:** the ToS grant is limited to *"through the Service"* — i.e. forking on GitHub. It does **not** authorize a hosting company to redistribute a release binary. Your right to install a plugin on a customer's server comes **solely from the repo's own license**, which is exactly why the `/license` endpoint matters. **Rule: if `/license` returns null or `NOASSERTION`, treat it as all-rights-reserved — hot-link only, never cache or mirror.** GitHub's own ToS says nothing about caching or redistributing release assets either way.

This is the **only** source in this entire long tail with real license metadata, which makes it disproportionately valuable: it's also the license oracle for ficsit (`source_url`) and Vintage Story (`sourcecodeurl`) when those point at GitHub.

## 10. mod.io ⭐ The most strategically important item here

A full commercial modding platform — API, SDKs, engine plugins, cross-platform + console, and **built-in monetization**. Unlike everything else in this list, it is *designed* to be integrated by third parties.

**Base:** `https://api.mod.io/v1` (plus regional `https://*.modapi.io/v1`). Always JSON.

**Auth — ⚠️ mandatory, verified live.** There is no anonymous access:
```
GET https://api.mod.io/v1/games            → 401 {"error_ref":11000,"message":"malformed/missing api_key"}
GET https://api.mod.io/v1/games?api_key=test → 401 {"error_ref":11001}
```
Two modes:
- **API key** (`?api_key=…`) — **GET only**, read/browse/download.
- **OAuth2** (`Authorization: Bearer …`) — full read+write, tokens *"valid for a common year"* (~365 days).

**Rate limits — exact, and the tiering matters enormously to you:**

| Scope | Limit |
|---|---|
| API key **linked to a game** | **unlimited** |
| API key **linked to a user** | **60 / minute** |
| OAuth2 user token | 120 / minute |
| OAuth2 user token, writes | 60 / minute |
| Per IP | 1,000 / minute |
| Per IP, writes | 60 / minute |

Exceeding → `429` with a `retry-after` header (seconds).

**⚠️ The unlimited tier requires being the game's publisher.** As a hosting company you get a *user-linked* key → **60/min**. That's fine for on-demand installs, thin for bulk catalog sync. Build an incremental sync on `date_updated` rather than full crawls, and cache aggressively. The 1,000/min per-IP ceiling is generous enough that a small worker pool is fine.

**Key endpoints:** `GET /games`, `GET /games/{id}`, `GET /games/{game_id}/mods`, `GET /games/{game_id}/mods/{mod_id}`, `GET /games/{game_id}/mods/{mod_id}/files`, `GET …/files/{file_id}`, plus subscribe/unsubscribe and full write CRUD under OAuth. Collections return `{data[], result_count, result_limit, result_offset, result_total}` — proper offset pagination, and rich filtering/sorting on almost every field.

**Fields:** `id, mod_id, game_id, name, summary` (both localizable), `status, visible` (0=hidden, 1=public), `date_added, date_updated, date_scanned`, `logo` (image object with multiple resolutions), media arrays for images/videos, and per-file `filesize, filehash` (MD5), `filename, version, changelog, metadata_blob`.

**Downloads:** each modfile carries a `download` object with **`binary_url` and `date_expires`** — i.e. **time-limited signed URLs**, same pattern as GitHub assets. Resolve at install time; never persist. `filehash` (MD5) lets you verify.

> **No dedicated license field.** `metadata_blob` (comma-separated key-values) is where an author *might* put one, but it's free-form and unreliable. Same gap as everywhere else. Games can define structured metadata/tag schemas, so per-game a "license" tag may exist — check per game, don't assume.

**ToS — [mod.io/legal/terms](https://mod.io/legal/terms), retrieved verbatim (30 KB). This is the most third-party-friendly position of anything researched:**

> "**User Generated Content is publicly available information which is shared with other users, other third parties, and is made available through the mod.io API** and you bear the risks involved with such public disclosures."

That clause explicitly contemplates third-party API consumption — a materially better legal footing than ficsit or Vintage Story.

The creator-side grant (§ on UGC):
> "You grant mod.io and the Relevant Game Admin a transferable, sublicensable, royalty-free, non-revocable, non-exclusive, perpetual, worldwide right to use, reproduce, process, modify, create derivative works from, distribute, transmit, transcode, translate, store, publicly perform, and otherwise communicate and display and distribute all such User Generated Content **for the sole purpose of providing the Services**…"

Note "for the sole purpose of providing the Services" — the grant runs to mod.io and the game publisher, **not** to you. So the same rule applies: **install on behalf of a user via the API; do not build a mirror.**

Also relevant:
> "1.2. The 'Services' means the services that mod.io Pty Ltd… operates and makes available to end users (you) through the mod.io website, **API, SDK**, official engine plugins, tools and any related services."

> "9.3. You acknowledge that if you copy, imitate, reproduce, reverse engineer, sell, retransmit, distribute, disseminate, publish, broadcast, circulate or exploit any Services Intellectual Property, you will be in breach of these Terms of Use…" — note this covers *mod.io's own* IP (site, branding, Game Data incl. logos/icons/screenshots), so be careful reusing their imagery in your UI.

The [Acceptable Use Policy](https://mod.io/legal/aup) is short and contains **no anti-scraping, anti-automation, anti-caching, or anti-crawling clause** — only prohibitions on unlawful use and on "attempts to interfere with another user's use or enjoyment of the Services, including blocking or disrupting access." Automated API use within rate limits is not restricted. mod.io Pty Ltd is Australian (ACN 628 999 039), DMCA-compliant, with takedown at `copyright@mod.io`.

There's also a **Monetization Terms** regime (`mod.io/monetization`) with Creators, **Resellers**, and "Enhanced License Rights" for "sale, resale, transfer of access." **If you ever want to bundle premium mods into hosting plans, that Reseller framework is the sanctioned route** — and it's the only such route anywhere in this research. Worth a conversation with mod.io directly; they sell "mod.io for Studios" and are commercially motivated to work with hosts.

**⚠️ Could not verify:** which specific games use mod.io. It needs an API key to enumerate `/games`, and searching surfaced only Steam-Workshop-based competitors. **Get a free API key and run `GET /games?_limit=100` — that single call tells you your entire addressable mod.io surface**, and it's the highest-value 10 minutes of follow-up from this whole report.

## What I could not verify

1. **ficsit.app ToS verbatim** — SPA renders client-side (curl returns empty); `forums.ficsit.app/tos.html` mirror returned 503 on every attempt. The restrictive "personal use / not entitled to redistribute" clause is search-surfaced only. **Open it in a browser before finalizing Satisfactory caching policy** — it's the single clause most likely to change your architecture.
2. **mod.io live responses and the games list** — requires an API key.
3. **Valheim `start_server_bepinex.sh` internals** — no primary source retrieved (BepInEx docs cover clients; Valheim wiki 402).
4. **ficsit-cli full command surface** — GitHub rate limit exhausted mid-research and `cli.ficsit.app` 301s straight to a Windows `.exe`. The dedicated-server docs cover the important part (SFTP/FTP/SMB + local, server must be stopped).
5. **Rate limits for ficsit and Vintage Story** — genuinely undocumented and unheadered. Not "none exist" — just unpublished.

## Three cross-cutting conclusions

**1. License metadata effectively does not exist outside GitHub.** ficsit (93 types introspected — zero license fields), Vintage Story (no key), mod.io (`metadata_blob` only), Steam Workshop, Nexus — none of them. If your catalog has a "License" column, it will be empty for most of the long tail. **Design the UI for "License: not provided by source — see mod page," and resolve via GitHub `/license` whenever `source_url`/`sourcecodeurl` points at GitHub.** That single fallback probably covers a meaningful share of Satisfactory and Vintage Story mods.

**2. Every source converges on the same legal posture: fetch-on-behalf-of-user, never mirror.** Vintage Story says it outright (a "mod user" includes someone downloading through a client; reuploads need the original license's permission). ficsit appears to say it more strictly. mod.io grants rights to itself and the publisher, not to you. GitHub's grant is limited to "through the Service." **Architect the installer as a just-in-time proxy that streams from origin to the customer's server at install time, with a short-lived local cache at most — not a mirror.** That one decision keeps you clean across all ten sources simultaneously. (It also happens to be why GitHub's and mod.io's expiring signed URLs aren't a problem: you were never going to persist them anyway.)

**3. The tiering for engineering effort is stark:**
- **Build now — real APIs, server-specific artifacts:** Satisfactory (`targets.LinuxServer` + `required_on_remote` is best-in-class), Vintage Story (`side` field is a free server filter), mod.io (get the key first, it may unlock several games at once).
- **Trivially easy, do it early:** ARK: Survival Ascended — the server self-updates from `-mods=`; you just write a launch arg.
- **Steam Workshop plumbing, no catalog work of its own:** Project Zomboid, tModLoader, Palworld. All three share one pattern: **download first, parse an internal manifest, then write config** (`mod.info` → `Mods=`; `.tmod` → `enabled.json`; `Info.json` → `IsServer`). Build that download-inspect-configure pipeline once and reuse it three times.

## 1. SpigotMC

### 1a. Official API — there IS one, contrary to the brief

You believed there is no official API. There are **two**, both undocumented-but-real:

**The "Simple API"** at `api.spigotmc.org/simple/0.2/` — I discovered its full action list by sending a bogus action:

```
$ curl "https://api.spigotmc.org/simple/0.2/index.php?action=bogus"
{"code":400,"message":"Invalid action. Valid actions: listResources, getResource,
 getResourcesByAuthor, listResourceCategories, getResourceUpdate, getResourceUpdates,
 getAuthor, findAuthor"}
```

Live `getResource` for LuckPerms (id 28140) returns clean JSON — and notably **it exposes `premium.price`/`premium.currency` and `external_download_url` directly**:

```json
{"id":28140,"title":"LuckPerms","current_version":"5.5.71",
 "category":{"id":21,"title":"Universal"},
 "supported_minecraft_versions":["1.7",...,"26.1","26.2"],
 "author":{"id":100356,"username":"Luck"},
 "premium":{"price":"0.00","currency":""},
 "stats":{"downloads":8915518,"updates":51,"reviews":{"unique":972,"total":1086},"rating":"4.7"},
 "external_download_url":"", "source_code_url":..., "donate_url":""}
```

For premium Citizens (13811): `"premium":{"price":"19.99","currency":"usd"}`, `category.title:"Premium"`.

**The legacy update endpoint** `api.spigotmc.org/legacy/update.php?resource=<id>` is live and returns a bare version string in `text/html`:

```
$ curl "https://api.spigotmc.org/legacy/update.php?resource=28140"
5.5.71
```

Version-check only, no download. Both these hosts are **not** behind the Cloudflare challenge that guards `www.spigotmc.org` — that's the practical reason they're usable.

**Caveat:** neither is publicly documented, neither carries a stated support commitment, and neither provides downloads. Treat as "official-ish, unsupported."

### 1b. Spiget (unofficial) — live field dump

`GET https://api.spiget.org/v2/resources?size=3` → HTTP 200. Pagination via headers, not body:

```
x-page-size: 3        x-page-index: 1
x-page-count: 30141   x-total: 90422
x-spiget-server: avocado
access-control-allow-origin: *
cache-control: max-age=1200
```

Corpus size from `/v2/status`: **90,422 resources, 119,130 authors, 544,479 versions, 28 categories.**

**Full field census** across 20 resources sorted by downloads:

```
author, category, contributors, donationLink, downloads, existenceStatus,
external, file, icon, id, likes, links, name, premium, price, currency,
rating, releaseDate, sourceCodeLink, supportedLanguages, tag, testedVersions,
updateDate, version
```

Detail endpoints add `description` (base64), `versions[]`, `updates[]`, `reviews[]`.

Live premium example (`/v2/resources/13811`, Citizens):
```json
{"external":false,
 "file":{"type":".jar","size":4.2,"sizeUnit":"MB","url":"resources/citizens.13811/download?version=652747"},
 "testedVersions":["1.21","26.1","26.2"],
 "rating":{"count":293,"average":3.8},
 "releaseDate":1445875920,"updateDate":1789671272,"downloads":28613,
 "premium":true,"price":19.99,"currency":"usd",
 "sourceCodeLink":"http://github.com/CitizensDev","existenceStatus":1,"id":13811}
```

`premium`/`price`/`currency` are **only populated on the detail endpoint and `/v2/resources/premium`** — in the list endpoint `price` and `currency` came back `None` even for premium rows. **Don't trust list-view premium flags; re-fetch detail before you offer anything as installable.** Some rows return `premium: null` rather than `false`, so treat null as unknown, not free.

`icon` returns both `icon.url` (relative, e.g. `data/resource_icons/28/28140.jpg?...`) and `icon.data` (base64 JPEG inline, ~1.8KB for author avatars). `links` is a map whose **keys are base64-encoded link labels** (`"R2l0aHVi"` = "GitHub"), with two stable literal keys: `discussion` and `additionalInformation`/`alternativeSupport`.

### 1c. Downloads — this is where Spiget breaks for your use case

Three distinct behaviors, all live-tested:

**Free + Spigot-hosted → works.** `/v2/resources/28140/download`:
```
302 → https://cdn.spiget.org/file/spiget-resources/28140.jar
200  content-type: application/java-archive  content-length: 1501521
file: Zip archive data  ✅ real jar
```

**External → returns an HTML web page, not a jar.** EssentialsX (9089) is `"external": true` with `file.type: "external"`, `file.size: 0`:
```
302 → https://github.com/EssentialsX/Essentials/releases/tag/2.22.0
200  content-type: text/html
```
That is the GitHub **release tag page**, not the asset. The `/download/proxy` variant returned 291KB of GitHub HTML too. An installer following this blindly writes an HTML file into the plugins directory. **You must branch on `external` before every download** — Spiget's own spec says so: *"The `external` field of a resource should be checked before downloading, to not receive any unexpected data"* ([swagger.yml L188](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpiGetOrg/Documentation/master/swagger.yml)).

**Premium → 404.** Citizens (13811), `premium:true`, non-external:
```
302 → https://cdn.spiget.org/file/spiget-resources/13811.jar
404  {"code":"not_found","message":"File with such name does not exist.","status":404}
```
Spiget does not mirror paid jars. Good — but it means premium entries are catalog-only dead ends.

**Version pinning is effectively broken.** This is the finding I'd flag hardest. `/download` (no version) hits the CDN and works. But `/versions/{id}/download` redirects to spigotmc.org itself and dies on the Cloudflare challenge:

```
$ curl -L "https://api.spiget.org/v2/resources/28140/versions/590885/download"
302 → https://spigotmc.org/resources/28140/download?version=590885
301 → https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/28140/download?version=590885
403  cf-mitigated: challenge   ("Just a moment...")
```

Same 403 for `versions/latest/download`. **Spiget can only reliably serve the single latest jar per resource**, from `cdn.spiget.org/file/spiget-resources/<id>.jar`. For a hosting installer where "pin the version that matches the customer's MC version" is table stakes, that's disqualifying on its own.

### 1d. No license field — confirmed

Correct, you suspected right. `license` appears **nowhere** in the Spiget schema — I grepped the swagger and censused live responses; the only `license` hit in swagger.yml is Spiget's *own* Apache-2.0 license in the `info` block. SpigotMC has no license field in its resource model at all: authors state licensing in prose inside the (base64) description, or not at all. There is no machine-readable licensing on this entire source. For a commercial catalog that is a serious gap — you cannot programmatically answer "am I allowed to redistribute/install this."

### 1e. Rate limits and operator risk

No `x-ratelimit-*` headers on any Spiget response. 20 rapid sequential requests: all 200. Spiget's swagger documents only a prose warning on the proxy download: *"Note: this endpoint has a pretty strict rate-limit - cache downloaded versions locally and avoid repeated requests."*

Operator: **inventivetalent** (`info@inventivetalent.org`), org [SpiGetOrg](https://github.com/SpiGetOrg), Apache-2.0. Maintenance is alive but thin — `api.spiget.org` last pushed 2025-09-21, `SpigetFetcher` 2025-12-19, `spiget.org` 2026-07-03. Several repos archived. Single-maintainer, hobby-funded (site credits JetBrains and Aternos as supporters).

**The risk signal I'd weight most:** the org contains a repo named **`spiget-puppeteer-client`**. Spiget gets its data by driving a headless browser against spigotmc.org to defeat Cloudflare. It is an adversarial scraper of a site that is actively blocking scrapers. That's a structurally fragile dependency — it breaks whenever Cloudflare tightens, and it puts you downstream of conduct SpigotMC explicitly prohibits.

### 1f. SpigotMC's legal position — verbatim

`www.spigotmc.org` is fully bot-hostile: **even `/robots.txt` returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare JS challenge.** WebFetch and curl with full browser headers both 403'd. I retrieved the text from the Wayback Machine.

From [Spigot Forum Rules](https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/spigot-rules/) (snapshot 2026-09-03, page dated Jul 19 2025):

> **"Do not distribute "Premium Resources" to those who have not purchased them."**

> **"Do not access the forums via automated mechanisms."**

> "Using pay-per-click sites such as adf.ly or similar services to distribute resources is forbidden. External resource download URLs must be a direct link."

> ""Premium Resources" are held to a higher standard of originality and have greater punishments associated with breaching of these rules."

> "Posting someone else's plugin or resource is not allowed. This includes minor edits such as configuration changes and code taken directly from tutorials or other resources."

From the [SpigotMC Terms of Service](https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/spigot-terms/) (snapshot 2025-12-03), §4 "Use of the Platform":

> **"You may not copy, distribute or disclose any part of the Platform in any medium, including without limitation by any automated or non-automated "scraping";"**

> **"You may not use any robot, spider, crawler, scraper or other automated means or interface not provided by us to access the Platform or to extract data;"**

> "You may not share your license or access with any other parties;"

§12 Intellectual Property:

> "You agree to not engage in the use, copying, or distribution anything contained within the Platform unless we have given express written permission."

**Read plainly:** SpigotMC prohibits scraping and prohibits third-party interfaces "not provided by us." Spiget is exactly such an interface. `api.spigotmc.org/simple/0.2/` and `/legacy/update.php`, by contrast, *are* provided by them — which is the one defensible reading for using those two while avoiding Spiget.

## 2. PaperMC Hangar — the strongest option

`https://hangar.papermc.io/api/v1/`, OpenAPI 3.1 spec at **`https://hangar.papermc.io/v3/api-docs`** (183KB; `/api-docs` is just a JS shell that WebFetch can't render).

### Live probes

`GET /api/v1/projects?limit=3` → 200. Body carries `{"pagination":{"count":3833,...},"result":[...]}` — **3,833 projects**, small and curatable vs Spigot's 90k.

Full project shape (live, ViaVersion):

```json
{"createdAt","publishedAt","id":31,
 "name":"ViaVersion","namespace":{"owner":"ViaVersion","slug":"ViaVersion"},
 "stats":{"views":1130308,"downloads":491008,"recentViews":39973,
          "recentDownloads":17549,"stars":468,"watchers":270},
 "category":"misc","description":"...","lastUpdated":"2026-09-18T15:01:51Z",
 "visibility":"public","userActions":{"starred","watching","flagged"},
 "settings":{
   "links":[{"id","type":"top|sidebar","title","links":[{"id","name","url"}]}],
   "tags":["SUPPORTS_FOLIA"],
   "license":{"name":null,"url":"https://github.com/.../LICENSE","type":"GPL"},
   "keywords":[...],"sponsors":null,"unlisted":false,
   "donation":{"subject":"","enable":false}},
 "supportedPlatforms":{"PAPER":[...],"WATERFALL":[...],"VELOCITY":[...]},
 "mainPageContent":"<full markdown>","memberNames":[...],
 "avatarUrl":"https://hangarcdn.papermc.io/avatars/project/31.webp?v=1"}
```

### License — confirmed yes, and well-populated

You believed yes; confirmed. Shape is `settings.license = {name, url, type}`. Census over the top 50 projects by downloads:

```
GPL + url        19      MIT + url         6      Other + url    3
Unspecified       7      MIT no url        5      AGPL + url     2
                         GPL no url        4      LGPL no url    2
                                                  Apache 2.0     1, LGPL+url 1
```

**43/50 (86%) carry a real SPDX-ish license type.** `name` is usually null and `type` is the field you want; `type:"Other"` means read `name`; `"Unspecified"` means the author didn't set one. This is the only source in this whole report with usable machine-readable licensing.

### Versions and downloads

`GET /api/v1/projects/ViaVersion/versions?limit=2` → 871 versions. Per-version payload is exactly what an installer needs:

```json
{"id":30415,"projectId":31,"name":"5.12.0","visibility":"public",
 "description":"<changelog markdown>",
 "stats":{"totalDownloads":860,"platformDownloads":{"PAPER":754,"VELOCITY":106}},
 "author":"kennytv","reviewState":"unreviewed",
 "channel":{"name":"Release","color":"#14b8a6","flags":["SENDS_NOTIFICATIONS","PINNED","FROZEN"]},
 "downloads":{"PAPER":{
    "fileInfo":{"name":"ViaVersion-5.12.0.jar","sizeBytes":6503775,
                "sha256Hash":"c4d512fa...f126be"},
    "externalUrl":null,
    "downloadUrl":"https://hangarcdn.papermc.io/plugins/ViaVersion/ViaVersion/versions/5.12.0/PAPER/ViaVersion-5.12.0.jar"}},
 "pluginDependencies":{"PAPER":[{"name":"ViaBackwards","projectId":12,"required":false,...}]},
 "platformDependencies":{...}}
```

**`sha256Hash` + `pluginDependencies` + per-platform `downloadUrl` is everything a real installer needs**, and Hangar gives it up anonymously.

**Unauthenticated download works — with one gotcha.** Sending `Accept: application/java-archive` returns **HTTP 406**. Send no `Accept`, or `Accept: */*`:

```
$ curl -L "https://hangar.papermc.io/api/v1/projects/ViaVersion/versions/5.12.0/PAPER/download"
301 → https://hangarcdn.papermc.io/plugins/.../ViaVersion-5.12.0.jar
200  application/java-archive  6503775 bytes
sha256 = c4d512fa9760fa41d17abaedde12aa1f4c9bde920d0a992fe0fc016962f126be  ✅ matches API exactly
```

Verified byte-for-byte against the API's advertised hash. The CDN URL also works directly (200, 6503775).

### Auth and rate limits — quoted from the spec's own `info.description`

> "There are two ways to consume the API: Authenticated or anonymous. **When using anonymous authentication, you only have access to public information**, but you don't need to worry about creating and storing an API key or handing JWTs."

> "Send a `POST` request with your API key identifier to `/api/v1/authenticate?apiKey=yourKey`. The response will contain your JWT as well as an expiration time. Put this JWT into the `Authorization` header of every request and make sure to request a new JWT after the expiration time has passed."

> "**Please also set a meaningful `User-Agent` header.** This allows us to better identify loads and needs for potentially new endpoints."

> "### Rate Limits and Caching — **The default rate limit is set at 20 requests every 5 seconds with an initial overdraft for extra leniency.** Individual endpoints, such as version creation, may have stricter rate limiting. **If applicable, always cache responses.** The Hangar API itself is cached by CloudFlare and internally."

> "Note that all routes **not** listed here should be considered **internal**, and can change at a moment's notice. **Do not use them.**"

Confirmed live: `POST /api/v1/authenticate` with no key → `{"title":"Bad Request","status":400,"detail":"Required parameter 'apiKey' is not present."}`. 20 rapid GETs all returned 200. No `x-ratelimit-*` headers exposed — the documented 20/5s is your only signal, so self-throttle.

**Rate limits are identical for anonymous and authenticated** — auth buys you private content and write access, not throughput.

### Two endpoints worth designing around

- **`GET /api/v1/versions/hash/{sha256}`** — reverse-lookup a jar by hash. Verified live: feeding ViaVersion's sha256 returned the full project. This lets you identify plugins a customer uploaded manually, detect outdated installs, and spot tampered jars. No other source offers this.
- **`GET /api/v1/platforms/{platform}/versions`** — authoritative MC version list per platform, with `subVersions` grouping (`26.3`, `26.2`, `26.1`→`[26.1.2,26.1.1,26.1]`, `1.21`→`[1.21.11…1.21]`). Use this to build your compatibility matrix rather than parsing Spigot's freeform `testedVersions` strings.

Also available: `/latest`, `/latestrelease`, `/stats`, `/members`, `/stargazers`, `/watchers`, `/pages/main/{project}`.

### Hangar legal

[Hangar Terms](https://hangar.papermc.io/terms): **no clauses at all** about API use, automated access, scraping, caching, redistribution, or commercial use. Creators retain rights — *"You retain any and all of Your rights to any Content You submit, post, or display on or through the Service"* — and grant Hangar *"the right and license to use, modify, publicly perform, publicly display, reproduce, and distribute such Content on and through the Service."* Note that grant is scoped to *"on and through the Service"*, so your right to redistribute a given jar comes from **that project's own license**, not from Hangar. Which is exactly why the `settings.license` field matters.

[Hangar Guidelines](https://hangar.papermc.io/guidelines): *"You are not allowed to re-upload resources of other authors as-is."* And critically for you — **paid plugins are banned outright**: *"Functionality may not be hidden behind a paywall or an author-granted license key."* So **everything on Hangar is free by policy.** No premium-flag logic needed. No rules governing third parties who index or mirror.

PaperMC's other legal pages live at [forums.papermc.io/help/terms](https://forums.papermc.io/help/terms/), `/help/privacy-policy/`, `/help/legal-notice/`.

## 3. Bukkit / dev.bukkit.org

**Confirmed CurseForge/Overwolf property.** `dev.bukkit.org/projects/worldedit` returns 200 with `<title>Overview - WorldEdit for Bukkit - Bukkit Plugins - Projects - Bukkit</title>` and links to `curseforge.com/store`, `legacy.curseforge.com/minecraft/bukkit-plugins/worldedit`, `curseforge-ideas.overwolf.com`, `support.curseforge.com`. It's a skinned CurseForge front-end. (`bukkit.org` itself 403s.)

In the CurseForge v1 API, Minecraft is `gameId=432` and Bukkit plugins are the `bukkit-plugins` class. I **could not verify the numeric `classId`** — `/v1/categories?gameId=432&classesOnly=true` requires a key and returned empty; `/v1/games` and `/v1/mods/search` both returned **403 "Forbidden: API Key missing or invalid"**. You'll need a key to confirm it; query `GET /v1/categories?gameId=432&classesOnly=true` once you have one. Community sources widely cite `classId=5` for Bukkit plugins but I could not confirm that live, so treat it as unverified.

Per [CurseForge docs](https://docs.curseforge.com/rest-api/), third-party keys are **approval-gated**: *"Not a game developer? If you're running a 3rd party modding service, we have an API solution for you. Click here to apply for a key."* There is also an `allowModDistribution` flag in the mod schema — authors can opt out of third-party distribution, and when they do you get metadata but no download URL. Budget for that: it's the single biggest operational gotcha with CurseForge for an installer.

### The ServerMods API is **still alive** — and current

This was the biggest surprise of the research. The old `api.curseforge.com/servermods/` endpoints respond, **with no API key at all**:

```
$ curl "https://api.curseforge.com/servermods/projects?search=vault"
[{"id":33184,"name":"Vault","slug":"vault","stage":"release"},
 {"id":33437,"name":"Vault Slots",...}, ...]

$ curl "https://api.curseforge.com/servermods/files?projectIds=31043"   # WorldEdit
→ 97 files, newest:
2026-06-16 | worldedit-bukkit-7.4.5.jar | gameVersion: 26.2 | release
  downloadUrl: https://files.forgecdn.net/files/8607/421/worldedit-bukkit-7.4.5.jar
```

Fields: `dateReleased, downloadUrl, fileName, fileUrl, gameVersion, md5, name, projectId, releaseType`.

**It is current, not frozen** — WorldEdit 7.4.5 for MC 26.2, released 2026-06-16. And the CDN URL serves a real jar unauthenticated:

```
$ curl -L "https://files.forgecdn.net/files/8607/421/worldedit-bukkit-7.4.5.jar"
HTTP 200  application/java-archive  7708742 bytes  ✅
```

15 rapid requests: all 200, no rate-limit headers. Two endpoints: `/servermods/projects?search=<q>` and `/servermods/files?projectIds=<id>[,<id>]`.

Caveats before you lean on it: it is **undocumented, unversioned, and un-deprecated only by inertia** — the [Bukkit wiki page](https://bukkit.fandom.com/wiki/ServerMods_API) is on Fandom, i.e. abandoned. It has **no license field** and no premium concept. Coverage is BukkitDev-era only — `search=luckperms` returned just "EasyLuckPerms", so modern plugins that never used BukkitDev aren't there. **Excellent for the long tail of classic Bukkit plugins; useless for anything post-2016.** Treat it as free upside with a fallback path, not a foundation.

## 4. Planet Minecraft — **do not build on this**

**No public API.** No documented endpoints, no JSON feed, no RSS. Site blocks automated access: WebFetch 403.

Content types are also mostly wrong for a *server-side plugin* installer: Maps, Player Skins, Texture Packs, Data Packs, Mob Skins, Mods, Blogs, Banners, Papercraft, Servers, Collections. The only server-relevant categories are Maps/worlds and Data Packs. Downloads route through site pages, not direct links.

The [Terms of Use](https://www.planetminecraft.com/terms_of_use/) (last modified January 4, 2020; © Cyprezz LLC) are about as hostile to your use case as terms get. Verbatim, from "General Site Use" — *"you agree that you shall not:"*

> **"5: Collect information about other visitors to our website without their consent or otherwise systematically extract data or data fields, including without limitation any financial data or e-mail addresses;"**

> **"6: Sell access to or the use of this website, including any content contained on, downloaded or accessed from this website, except as specifically permitted in writing by Planet Minecraft;"**

> **"7: Redistribute any content, including data, provided by us in any manner whatsoever including by means of printed publication, fax broadcast, web pages, e-mail, web newsgroups or forums, or any other electronic or paper-based service or method;"**

> **"8: Intentionally alter the format in which site data is provided by us or otherwise circumvent our regular interfaces to such data; and"**

> **"9: Embed or import any site data provided by us into any information services (whether or not web-based), data files or application software, including without limitation episode index systems, except as except as specifically permitted in writing by Planet Minecraft."**

> "2: Disrupt, place unreasonable burdens or excessive loads on, interfere with or attempt to gain unauthorized access to any portion of our website…"

Clauses 5, 7, 8 and 9 each independently prohibit building a catalog from PMC. Clause 6 prohibits selling access to content obtained from it. **A commercial hosting catalog sourcing PMC is a direct, multi-clause breach.** They also run an active DMCA program with a named agent (Maxwell Langdon, Cyprezz LLC) and a repeat-infringer termination policy under 17 U.S.C. §512(i). My recommendation: exclude entirely, and don't route around it with a "user pastes a URL" flow either, since clause 9 covers importing site data into application software.

### BuiltByBit (formerly MC-Market)

Official REST API at `api.builtbybit.com` — **auth required on every call**:
```
$ curl "https://api.builtbybit.com/v1/health"
{"result":"error","error":{"code":"HeaderMissingError",
 "message":"The 'Authorization' header was not present."}}
```
Response header `authenticated: false`. Docs at [builtbybit.com/wiki/ultimate-api](https://builtbybit.com/wiki/ultimate-api/) (V1, V2, and OAuth2 documentation).

[Terms of Service](https://builtbybit.com/wiki/terms) §2 "ACCESSING OUR SERVICES", verbatim:

> **"Our Services includes a REST API through which we allow certain users certain levels of access to various information made available through our Services. Any sort of automated interfacing with our Services outside of our REST API is prohibited unless explicit permission is granted. Moreover, you agree not to crawl or scrape our Services for information, nor to utilize information made available through our Services in reproducing or reconstructing areas of our Services externally without explicit permission from us."**

That last clause — *"reproducing or reconstructing areas of our Services externally"* — is **a plugin catalog, described exactly.** Even using their sanctioned API, mirroring their marketplace into your catalog needs explicit written permission. Also relevant: sellers grant BBB *"a perpetual, unlimited, non-exclusive, royalty free license to host, copy, modify, distribute, sell and sublicense"* their content — that license runs to BBB, not to you.

It's a paid marketplace: downloads are purchaser-scoped. **Not catalogable without a partnership conversation.** They do maintain wiki pages on "Redistribution rights", "Server jar policies", "Anti-leak policies" and "Resource EULAs" that would be worth reading if you pursue this — I could not extract their bodies (JS-gated in Wayback snapshots; only navigation chrome rendered).

### Jenkins CI — live and genuinely useful

The right primary source for the ~50 open-source plugins that matter most — and the real home of most Spigot `external:true` resources (EssentialsX, ViaVersion, SkinsRestorer, ViaBackwards all point there). ## Recommendation

**Build the catalog on Hangar + GitHub Releases + PaperMC Fill v3, and add ServerMods as free long-tail coverage.** That set gives you machine-readable licenses (Hangar/GitHub), sha256 or md5 verification (Hangar/Fill/ServerMods), real dependency metadata (Hangar), anonymous access, documented rate limits, and no terms that prohibit what you're doing. Hangar is small (3,833 projects) but it's the curated, free-by-policy, legally clean core — and its hash-lookup endpoint gives you a genuine feature nobody else can.

**Treat SpigotMC as metadata-only, via the official `simple/0.2` API, and do not ship Spiget-backed installs.** Three independent reasons, any one sufficient: SpigotMC's ToS prohibits third-party scraping interfaces in terms that name exactly what Spiget is; there is no license field anywhere in the source, so you cannot establish a right to redistribute; and version-pinned downloads are simply broken (403 behind Cloudflare), leaving you able to serve only each plugin's latest jar. If you want Spigot-discovered plugins installable, resolve them to GitHub Releases by `sourceCodeLink` and install from there — that converts a legally and technically shaky path into a clean one.

**Exclude Planet Minecraft.** Five separate ToS clauses prohibit it, and they enforce.

The one item I'd action before anything else: **your installer's PaperMC integration is on a sunset API.** `api.papermc.io/v2` returns `{"ok":false,"error":"sunset"}` for paper, velocity, waterfall and folia. Migrate to `fill.papermc.io/v3` and add the mandatory identifying User-Agent — without it you're non-compliant with their stated policy, and the old endpoints are already returning errors rather than jars.</result>

## 1. SpigotMC

### 1a. Official API — there IS one, contrary to the brief

You believed there is no official API. There are **two**, both undocumented-but-real:

**The "Simple API"** at `api.spigotmc.org/simple/0.2/` — I discovered its full action list by sending a bogus action:

```
$ curl "https://api.spigotmc.org/simple/0.2/index.php?action=bogus"
{"code":400,"message":"Invalid action. Valid actions: listResources, getResource,
 getResourcesByAuthor, listResourceCategories, getResourceUpdate, getResourceUpdates,
 getAuthor, findAuthor"}
```

Live `getResource` for LuckPerms (id 28140) returns clean JSON — and notably **it exposes `premium.price`/`premium.currency` and `external_download_url` directly**:

```json
{"id":28140,"title":"LuckPerms","current_version":"5.5.71",
 "category":{"id":21,"title":"Universal"},
 "supported_minecraft_versions":["1.7",...,"26.1","26.2"],
 "author":{"id":100356,"username":"Luck"},
 "premium":{"price":"0.00","currency":""},
 "stats":{"downloads":8915518,"updates":51,"reviews":{"unique":972,"total":1086},"rating":"4.7"},
 "external_download_url":"", "source_code_url":..., "donate_url":""}
```

For premium Citizens (13811): `"premium":{"price":"19.99","currency":"usd"}`, `category.title:"Premium"`.

**The legacy update endpoint** `api.spigotmc.org/legacy/update.php?resource=<id>` is live and returns a bare version string in `text/html`:

```
$ curl "https://api.spigotmc.org/legacy/update.php?resource=28140"
5.5.71
```

Version-check only, no download. Both these hosts are **not** behind the Cloudflare challenge that guards `www.spigotmc.org` — that's the practical reason they're usable.

**Caveat:** neither is publicly documented, neither carries a stated support commitment, and neither provides downloads. Treat as "official-ish, unsupported."

### 1b. Spiget (unofficial) — live field dump

`GET https://api.spiget.org/v2/resources?size=3` → HTTP 200. Pagination via headers, not body:

```
x-page-size: 3        x-page-index: 1
x-page-count: 30141   x-total: 90422
x-spiget-server: avocado
access-control-allow-origin: *
cache-control: max-age=1200
```

Corpus size from `/v2/status`: **90,422 resources, 119,130 authors, 544,479 versions, 28 categories.**

**Full field census** across 20 resources sorted by downloads:

```
author, category, contributors, donationLink, downloads, existenceStatus,
external, file, icon, id, likes, links, name, premium, price, currency,
rating, releaseDate, sourceCodeLink, supportedLanguages, tag, testedVersions,
updateDate, version
```

Detail endpoints add `description` (base64), `versions[]`, `updates[]`, `reviews[]`.

Live premium example (`/v2/resources/13811`, Citizens):
```json
{"external":false,
 "file":{"type":".jar","size":4.2,"sizeUnit":"MB","url":"resources/citizens.13811/download?version=652747"},
 "testedVersions":["1.21","26.1","26.2"],
 "rating":{"count":293,"average":3.8},
 "releaseDate":1445875920,"updateDate":1789671272,"downloads":28613,
 "premium":true,"price":19.99,"currency":"usd",
 "sourceCodeLink":"http://github.com/CitizensDev","existenceStatus":1,"id":13811}
```

`premium`/`price`/`currency` are **only populated on the detail endpoint and `/v2/resources/premium`** — in the list endpoint `price` and `currency` came back `None` even for premium rows. **Don't trust list-view premium flags; re-fetch detail before you offer anything as installable.** Some rows return `premium: null` rather than `false`, so treat null as unknown, not free.

`icon` returns both `icon.url` (relative, e.g. `data/resource_icons/28/28140.jpg?...`) and `icon.data` (base64 JPEG inline, ~1.8KB for author avatars). `links` is a map whose **keys are base64-encoded link labels** (`"R2l0aHVi"` = "GitHub"), with two stable literal keys: `discussion` and `additionalInformation`/`alternativeSupport`.

### 1c. Downloads — this is where Spiget breaks for your use case

Three distinct behaviors, all live-tested:

**Free + Spigot-hosted → works.** `/v2/resources/28140/download`:
```
302 → https://cdn.spiget.org/file/spiget-resources/28140.jar
200  content-type: application/java-archive  content-length: 1501521
file: Zip archive data  ✅ real jar
```

**External → returns an HTML web page, not a jar.** EssentialsX (9089) is `"external": true` with `file.type: "external"`, `file.size: 0`:
```
302 → https://github.com/EssentialsX/Essentials/releases/tag/2.22.0
200  content-type: text/html
```
That is the GitHub **release tag page**, not the asset. The `/download/proxy` variant returned 291KB of GitHub HTML too. An installer following this blindly writes an HTML file into the plugins directory. **You must branch on `external` before every download** — Spiget's own spec says so: *"The `external` field of a resource should be checked before downloading, to not receive any unexpected data"* ([swagger.yml L188](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpiGetOrg/Documentation/master/swagger.yml)).

**Premium → 404.** Citizens (13811), `premium:true`, non-external:
```
302 → https://cdn.spiget.org/file/spiget-resources/13811.jar
404  {"code":"not_found","message":"File with such name does not exist.","status":404}
```
Spiget does not mirror paid jars. Good — but it means premium entries are catalog-only dead ends.

**Version pinning is effectively broken.** This is the finding I'd flag hardest. `/download` (no version) hits the CDN and works. But `/versions/{id}/download` redirects to spigotmc.org itself and dies on the Cloudflare challenge:

```
$ curl -L "https://api.spiget.org/v2/resources/28140/versions/590885/download"
302 → https://spigotmc.org/resources/28140/download?version=590885
301 → https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/28140/download?version=590885
403  cf-mitigated: challenge   ("Just a moment...")
```

Same 403 for `versions/latest/download`. **Spiget can only reliably serve the single latest jar per resource**, from `cdn.spiget.org/file/spiget-resources/<id>.jar`. For a hosting installer where "pin the version that matches the customer's MC version" is table stakes, that's disqualifying on its own.

### 1d. No license field — confirmed

Correct, you suspected right. `license` appears **nowhere** in the Spiget schema — I grepped the swagger and censused live responses; the only `license` hit in swagger.yml is Spiget's *own* Apache-2.0 license in the `info` block. SpigotMC has no license field in its resource model at all: authors state licensing in prose inside the (base64) description, or not at all. There is no machine-readable licensing on this entire source. For a commercial catalog that is a serious gap — you cannot programmatically answer "am I allowed to redistribute/install this."

### 1e. Rate limits and operator risk

No `x-ratelimit-*` headers on any Spiget response. 20 rapid sequential requests: all 200. Spiget's swagger documents only a prose warning on the proxy download: *"Note: this endpoint has a pretty strict rate-limit - cache downloaded versions locally and avoid repeated requests."*

Operator: **inventivetalent** (`info@inventivetalent.org`), org [SpiGetOrg](https://github.com/SpiGetOrg), Apache-2.0. Maintenance is alive but thin — `api.spiget.org` last pushed 2025-09-21, `SpigetFetcher` 2025-12-19, `spiget.org` 2026-07-03. Several repos archived. Single-maintainer, hobby-funded (site credits JetBrains and Aternos as supporters).

**The risk signal I'd weight most:** the org contains a repo named **`spiget-puppeteer-client`**. Spiget gets its data by driving a headless browser against spigotmc.org to defeat Cloudflare. It is an adversarial scraper of a site that is actively blocking scrapers. That's a structurally fragile dependency — it breaks whenever Cloudflare tightens, and it puts you downstream of conduct SpigotMC explicitly prohibits.

### 1f. SpigotMC's legal position — verbatim

`www.spigotmc.org` is fully bot-hostile: **even `/robots.txt` returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare JS challenge.** WebFetch and curl with full browser headers both 403'd. I retrieved the text from the Wayback Machine.

From [Spigot Forum Rules](https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/spigot-rules/) (snapshot 2026-09-03, page dated Jul 19 2025):

> **"Do not distribute "Premium Resources" to those who have not purchased them."**

> **"Do not access the forums via automated mechanisms."**

> "Using pay-per-click sites such as adf.ly or similar services to distribute resources is forbidden. External resource download URLs must be a direct link."

> ""Premium Resources" are held to a higher standard of originality and have greater punishments associated with breaching of these rules."

> "Posting someone else's plugin or resource is not allowed. This includes minor edits such as configuration changes and code taken directly from tutorials or other resources."

From the [SpigotMC Terms of Service](https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/spigot-terms/) (snapshot 2025-12-03), §4 "Use of the Platform":

> **"You may not copy, distribute or disclose any part of the Platform in any medium, including without limitation by any automated or non-automated "scraping";"**

> **"You may not use any robot, spider, crawler, scraper or other automated means or interface not provided by us to access the Platform or to extract data;"**

> "You may not share your license or access with any other parties;"

§12 Intellectual Property:

> "You agree to not engage in the use, copying, or distribution anything contained within the Platform unless we have given express written permission."

**Read plainly:** SpigotMC prohibits scraping and prohibits third-party interfaces "not provided by us." Spiget is exactly such an interface. `api.spigotmc.org/simple/0.2/` and `/legacy/update.php`, by contrast, *are* provided by them — which is the one defensible reading for using those two while avoiding Spiget.

`GET /api/v1/projects/ViaVersion/versions?limit=2` → 871 versions. Per-version payload is exactly what an installer needs:

**`sha256Hash` + `pluginDependencies` + per-platform `downloadUrl` is everything a real installer needs**, and Hangar gives it up anonymously.

**Unauthenticated download works — with one gotcha.** Sending `Accept: application/java-archive` returns **HTTP 406**. Send no `Accept`, or `Accept: */*`:

```
$ curl -L "https://hangar.papermc.io/api/v1/projects/ViaVersion/versions/5.12.0/PAPER/download"
301 → https://hangarcdn.papermc.io/plugins/.../ViaVersion-5.12.0.jar

sha256 = c4d512fa9760fa41d17abaedde12aa1f4c9bde920d0a992fe0fc016962f126be  ✅ matches API exactly
```

Verified byte-for-byte against the API's advertised hash. The CDN URL also works directly (200, 6503775).

### Auth and rate limits — quoted from the spec's own `info.description`

> "There are two ways to consume the API: Authenticated or anonymous. **When using anonymous authentication, you only have access to public information**, but you don't need to worry about creating and storing an API key or handing JWTs."

> "Send a `POST` request with your API key identifier to `/api/v1/authenticate?apiKey=yourKey`. The response will contain your JWT as well as an expiration time. Put this JWT into the `Authorization` header of every request and make sure to request a new JWT after the expiration time has passed."

> "**Please also set a meaningful `User-Agent` header.** This allows us to better identify loads and needs for potentially new endpoints."

> "### Rate Limits and Caching — **The default rate limit is set at 20 requests every 5 seconds with an initial overdraft for extra leniency.** Individual endpoints, such as version creation, may have stricter rate limiting. **If applicable, always cache responses.** The Hangar API itself is cached by CloudFlare and internally."

> "Note that all routes **not** listed here should be considered **internal**, and can change at a moment's notice. **Do not use them.**"

Confirmed live: `POST /api/v1/authenticate` with no key → `{"title":"Bad Request","status":400,"detail":"Required parameter 'apiKey' is not present."}`. 20 rapid GETs all returned 200. No `x-ratelimit-*` headers exposed — the documented 20/5s is your only signal, so self-throttle.

**Rate limits are identical for anonymous and authenticated** — auth buys you private content and write access, not throughput.

### Two endpoints worth designing around

- **`GET /api/v1/versions/hash/{sha256}`** — reverse-lookup a jar by hash. Verified live: feeding ViaVersion's sha256 returned the full project. This lets you identify plugins a customer uploaded manually, detect outdated installs, and spot tampered jars. No other source offers this.
- **`GET /api/v1/platforms/{platform}/versions`** — authoritative MC version list per platform, with `subVersions` grouping (`26.3`, `26.2`, `26.1`→`[26.1.2,26.1.1,26.1]`, `1.21`→`[1.21.11…1.21]`). Use this to build your compatibility matrix rather than parsing Spigot's freeform `testedVersions` strings.

Also available: `/latest`, `/latestrelease`, `/stats`, `/members`, `/stargazers`, `/watchers`, `/pages/main/{project}`.

### Hangar legal

[Hangar Terms](https://hangar.papermc.io/terms): **no clauses at all** about API use, automated access, scraping, caching, redistribution, or commercial use. Creators retain rights — *"You retain any and all of Your rights to any Content You submit, post, or display on or through the Service"* — and grant Hangar *"the right and license to use, modify, publicly perform, publicly display, reproduce, and distribute such Content on and through the Service."* Note that grant is scoped to *"on and through the Service"*, so your right to redistribute a given jar comes from **that project's own license**, not from Hangar. Which is exactly why the `settings.license` field matters.

[Hangar Guidelines](https://hangar.papermc.io/guidelines): *"You are not allowed to re-upload resources of other authors as-is."* And critically for you — **paid plugins are banned outright**: *"Functionality may not be hidden behind a paywall or an author-granted license key."* So **everything on Hangar is free by policy.** No premium-flag logic needed. No rules governing third parties who index or mirror.

PaperMC's other legal pages live at [forums.papermc.io/help/terms](https://forums.papermc.io/help/terms/), `/help/privacy-policy/`, `/help/legal-notice/`.

                "26.3":["26.3","26.3-rc-3"],"26.2":["26.2","26.2-rc-2"],
                "26.1":["26.1.2","26.1.1"],"1.21":[...21 entries...],...}}]}

$ curl https://fill.papermc.io/v3/projects/paper/versions/26.3/builds/latest
{"id":19,"time":"2026-09-18T20:29:40Z","channel":"ALPHA",
 "commits":[{"sha":"b4c7d168...","time":"...","message":"..."}],

   "name":"paper-26.3-19.jar",

And, directly relevant to an auto-updating hosting panel:

> "**We emphatically do not recommend using unstable builds or auto-updaters within production environments.**"

No documented rate limits or caching policy for Fill.

## 3. Bukkit / dev.bukkit.org

**Confirmed CurseForge/Overwolf property.** `dev.bukkit.org/projects/worldedit` returns 200 with `<title>Overview - WorldEdit for Bukkit - Bukkit Plugins - Projects - Bukkit</title>` and links to `curseforge.com/store`, `legacy.curseforge.com/minecraft/bukkit-plugins/worldedit`, `curseforge-ideas.overwolf.com`, `support.curseforge.com`. It's a skinned CurseForge front-end. (`bukkit.org` itself 403s.)

In the CurseForge v1 API, Minecraft is `gameId=432` and Bukkit plugins are the `bukkit-plugins` class. I **could not verify the numeric `classId`** — `/v1/categories?gameId=432&classesOnly=true` requires a key and returned empty; `/v1/games` and `/v1/mods/search` both returned **403 "Forbidden: API Key missing or invalid"**. You'll need a key to confirm it; query `GET /v1/categories?gameId=432&classesOnly=true` once you have one. Community sources widely cite `classId=5` for Bukkit plugins but I could not confirm that live, so treat it as unverified.

Per [CurseForge docs](https://docs.curseforge.com/rest-api/), third-party keys are **approval-gated**: *"Not a game developer? If you're running a 3rd party modding service, we have an API solution for you. Click here to apply for a key."* There is also an `allowModDistribution` flag in the mod schema — authors can opt out of third-party distribution, and when they do you get metadata but no download URL. Budget for that: it's the single biggest operational gotcha with CurseForge for an installer.

### The ServerMods API is **still alive** — and current

This was the biggest surprise of the research. The old `api.curseforge.com/servermods/` endpoints respond, **with no API key at all**:

```
$ curl "https://api.curseforge.com/servermods/projects?search=vault"
[{"id":33184,"name":"Vault","slug":"vault","stage":"release"},
 {"id":33437,"name":"Vault Slots",...}, ...]

$ curl "https://api.curseforge.com/servermods/files?projectIds=31043"   # WorldEdit
→ 97 files, newest:
2026-06-16 | worldedit-bukkit-7.4.5.jar | gameVersion: 26.2 | release
  downloadUrl: https://files.forgecdn.net/files/8607/421/worldedit-bukkit-7.4.5.jar
```

Fields: `dateReleased, downloadUrl, fileName, fileUrl, gameVersion, md5, name, projectId, releaseType`.

**It is current, not frozen** — WorldEdit 7.4.5 for MC 26.2, released 2026-06-16. And the CDN URL serves a real jar unauthenticated:

```
$ curl -L "https://files.forgecdn.net/files/8607/421/worldedit-bukkit-7.4.5.jar"
HTTP 200  application/java-archive  7708742 bytes  ✅
```

15 rapid requests: all 200, no rate-limit headers. Two endpoints: `/servermods/projects?search=<q>` and `/servermods/files?projectIds=<id>[,<id>]`.

Caveats before you lean on it: it is **undocumented, unversioned, and un-deprecated only by inertia** — the [Bukkit wiki page](https://bukkit.fandom.com/wiki/ServerMods_API) is on Fandom, i.e. abandoned. It has **no license field** and no premium concept. Coverage is BukkitDev-era only — `search=luckperms` returned just "EasyLuckPerms", so modern plugins that never used BukkitDev aren't there. **Excellent for the long tail of classic Bukkit plugins; useless for anything post-2016.** Treat it as free upside with a fallback path, not a foundation.
