content.text:
All four research streams are complete. Here is the consolidated report.

---

# NxLabs source research — everything except Modrinth and Thunderstore

Live probes run 2026-09-19 from this box. Anything marked **TESTED** is a captured HTTP response.

---

## 1. Factorio Mod Portal — **green light, best-in-class metadata, one hard auth wall**

### (a) API
Base `https://mods.factorio.com/api`. Docs: https://wiki.factorio.com/Mod_portal_API

| Endpoint | Auth | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/mods` | none | **TESTED** — 23,317 mods. Params: `page`, `page_size` (int or `"max"`), `sort`, `sort_order`, `hide_deprecated`, `namelist[]`, `version` |
| `GET /api/mods?page_size=max` | none | **TESTED** — single 13.8 MB JSON, all 23,317 mods, 11 s. Returns `pagination: null` and only 8 short fields per mod |
| `GET /api/mods/{name}` | none | short info |
| `GET /api/mods/{name}/full` | none | **TESTED** — the one you want |
| `GET /api/mods?namelist=A&namelist=B` | none | **TESTED** — bulk; swaps `latest_release` for the full `releases[]` array. Best incremental-sync primitive |
| `POST /api/search` | **username+token required** | **TESTED** — 400 `{'username': ['Missing data for required field.'], 'token': [...]}` |
| `GET /api/bookmarks` | username+token | |

**`/api/mods/full` does not exist** — **TESTED**, returns 404 `{"message":"Mod not found"}` (it parses `full` as a mod name). Your brief listed it; it isn't real.

`sort` accepts only `name`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. **TESTED:** `sort=downloads_count` is silently ignored and falls back to name order. There is no popularity sort — you must sort client-side off the `page_size=max` dump.

### (b) Fields — and yes, real licence metadata
`/full` returns: `name, title, owner, summary, description, category, tags[], downloads_count, score, thumbnail, images[], homepage, source_url, github_path, license{}, created_at, updated_at, last_highlighted_at, changelog, releases[]`.

`license` object (**TESTED**, matches the wiki's documented table `id/name/title/description/url`):
```json
{"id":"default_gnulgplv3","name":"gnulgplv3","title":"GNU LGPLv3",
 "description":"Version 3 of the GNU LGPL is an additional set of permissions…",
 "url":"https://opensource.org/licenses/lgpl-3.0"}
```

**It is NOT SPDX.** Two shapes:
- `default_*` — a fixed enum. **TESTED** ids seen: `default_mit`, `default_gnugplv3`, `default_gnulgplv3`, `default_unlicense` (plus Apache-2.0, MPL-2.0, ISC, BSD-3-Clause observed by title).
- `custom_<24-hex-mongoid>` — **author-authored free text**. The `title` is whatever they typed. I observed `"CC_BY_NC_ND_4.0"`, `"CC BY-NC-ND 4.0"`, `"CC By-NC-ND 4.0"`, `" CC BY SA 4.0"`, `"See below"`, `"Unnamed license"`, `"Skrunix"`, `"MIT / CC BY-NC-ND 4.0"` — all as distinct license records. You need a normalisation table keyed on `license.id` (stable) not `title` (not stable).

**Images:** `thumbnail` is a **relative** path (`/assets/<sha1>.thumb.png`) — prefix `https://assets-mod.factorio.com`. **TESTED:** 200, CDN77, 145 KB. `images[]` entries are already absolute (`{id, thumbnail, url}`). **TESTED on a random 60-mod sample: 18/60 have no thumbnail and 21/60 have an empty `images[]`** — budget for a placeholder.

### (c) Download — **hard blocker, requires a Factorio licence**
`release.download_url` is a path (`/download/{name}/{release_id}`). **TESTED unauthenticated: 302 → `/login` → 302 → `factorio.com/login` → 403 Cloudflare challenge.** With dummy `?username=&token=`: **403**.

Wiki: *"Simply adding username and token parameters to the download url will prevent the redirecting."* Token comes from `player-data.json` → `service-token`, or from `POST https://auth.factorio.com/api-login` (**TESTED** — live, returns `{"data":{},"error":"login-failed",...}` for bad creds). Community docs are explicit: *"To be able to download a mod, being authenticated is required, and **the account needs to own a Factorio license**."*

⚠️ **Operational consequence:** NxLabs must hold a Factorio-owning account and put its service token into the installer, or ask each customer for theirs. Every release carries a `sha1` — verify it.

### (d) Rate limits
**None documented and none observed.** **TESTED:** 40 sequential `/full` requests at ~1.4 req/s → 40× HTTP 200, zero throttling, no `x-ratelimit-*` headers. Responses carry `Cache-Control: max-age=900, public` and **support conditional GET — TESTED: `If-Modified-Since` → HTTP 304**. Build the sync on 304s.

### (e) Legal — **this is where Factorio gets interesting**
[factorio.com/terms-of-service](https://www.factorio.com/terms-of-service):

> "You may use the free Factorio headless server to **run and operate a commercial service providing servers to players**. However we reserve the right to request the cessation of the service should an issue with the service provider arise."

That is explicit permission for your core business — better than any other publisher in this report.

> "By uploading a mod to the mod portal, you grant us the irrevocable right to reproduce, adapt and distribute the mod and its content **as necessary to operate the mod portal**…"

That grant runs to Wube, not to you. Nothing addresses third-party API use, caching, or automated access. **Your right to install a given mod comes from that mod's own `license` field.**

🚨 **And that is a problem at the top of the catalogue.** I sampled the **top 150 mods by download count** and resolved every licence:

```
MIT 52 | Limited Distribution Only Licence 35 | Copyright, Redistribution, No editing 18
CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 15 | GNU LGPLv3 12 | GNU GPLv3 8 | CC BY-NC 4.0 2 | …
→ custom (non-default) licences = 57.8% of all downloads in the top 150
```

I pulled the two dominant custom licences verbatim.

**FMLDOL** (Earendel — Space Exploration, AAI family; 35 of the top 150), from the Google Doc the API links:
> "**Commercial Use — No.** You are not allowed to make money off this mod or any of the contained assets."
> "You can distribute the complete and unmodified mod package with the following conditions: 1. The mod must not be modified… 2. **You must disclose the source by providing a link to the mod on the mod portal**… a link to Earendel's discord… and a link to Earendel's Patreon."

**bobingabout's licence** (18 of the top 150):
> "**No Commercial Use** - You are not allowed to make money off my work."
> "Distribution - You are allowed to redistribute my mods as is. This includes being repackaged as part of a mod pack."

Both permit unmodified redistribution but forbid commercial use. Whether "customer pays for hosting, mod installs for free" is "making money off the mod" is genuinely unsettled — but **the safe architecture is fetch-on-demand from mods.factorio.com under the customer's own credentials, never a Nxeon mirror**, plus rendering the attribution links FMLDOL requires.

**Headless install mechanics:** drop the **unextracted** `.zip` into `mods/`; `mod-list.json` controls enable/disable; `mod-settings.dat` holds runtime settings; **dependencies are not auto-resolved on a headless server** — you must walk `release.info_json.dependencies` yourself; **a full server restart is required**.

---

## 2. uMod / Oxide — **green light, cleanest API in the whole report**

### (a) API — undocumented but fully public, unauthenticated
| Endpoint | Result |
|---|---|
| `GET https://umod.org/plugins/search.json?page=N&sort=…&sortdir=…&categories[]=rust` | **TESTED** 200 |
| `GET https://umod.org/plugins/{slug}.json` | **TESTED** 200 |
| `GET https://umod.org/plugins/{Name}.cs` | **TESTED** 200 — raw C# source |
| `GET https://assets.umod.org/games.json` | **TESTED** 200 (umod.org/games.json 301s here) |

⚠️ **`per_page`/`limit` are ignored — TESTED, hard-locked at 10 results/page.** Corpus is 1,710 plugins total, so a full sync is 171 requests.

### (b) Fields — including a real `license`
```json
{"name":"ZoneVending","license":"mit","license_url":null,
 "icon_url":"https://assets.umod.org/images/icons/plugin/5f6bc6a5e8d0f.png",
 "title","slug","description","downloads":30724,"rating","category",
 "url","json_url","download_url":"https://umod.org/plugins/ZoneVending.cs",
 "distribution":"download","status_detail":{"value":1,"text":"Published"},
 "latest_release_version":"0.3.5","latest_release_version_checksum":"3ec194b6…",
 "latest_release_at","author","author_icon_url","author_id","tags_all","watchers"}
```

**Licence values are lowercase slugs, not SPDX.** **TESTED** across 26 top Rust plugins: `mit` ×18, `gpl3` ×4, **`null` ×4**. So ~15% carry no licence — treat null as all-rights-reserved.

`latest_release_version_checksum` (SHA-1) gives you free update detection and integrity checking. **TESTED** across 200 plugins: `distribution` is `"download"` and `status_detail.text` is `"Published"` for 200/200 — no external/premium/hidden variants in practice.

### (c) Download — **unauthenticated, trivially works**
**TESTED:** `GET https://umod.org/plugins/ZoneVending.cs` → 200, 3,573 bytes of C#. No auth, no referer, no cookie.

### (d) Rate limit — **hard 30 requests/minute**
**TESTED**, exact headers: `x-ratelimit-limit: 30`, `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, `retry-after: 15`, `x-ratelimit-reset: <unix>`, HTTP **429**. No `ETag`/`Last-Modified` (`cache-control: no-cache, private`), so **no conditional-GET shortcut** — full sync is ~6 minutes at the limit. Note `umod.org` HTML pages sit behind a Cloudflare JS challenge (**TESTED:** even `/robots.txt` 403s) but the `.json`/`.cs` endpoints pass cleanly.

### (e) Legal
[umod.org/terms](https://umod.org/terms) (effective Aug 23 2018, retrieved via Wayback since the live page is CF-challenged). The one clause that matters:

> "**Not to use any data from the Site in third-party applications directly competing with uMod.**"

A hosting-panel plugin browser is plausibly *complementary*, not competing — but it's a judgement call worth a one-line email to uMod. Nothing prohibits caching, scraping, or commercial use. Site footer: *"The uMod open-source projects licensed by their respective contributors."*

### Oxide / Carbon — how Rust plugins actually get installed
`assets.umod.org/games.json` is a gift — it hands you the install contract per game. **TESTED**, Rust entry:
```json
{"slug":"rust","server_appid":"258550","client_appid":"252490",
 "installation_paths":"RustDedicated_Data/Managed","target_framework":"v4.6",
 "snapshot_url":"https://github.com/OxideMod/Oxide.Rust/releases/download/2.0.7723/Oxide.Rust-linux.zip",
 "repository":"OxideMod/Oxide.Rust","latest_release_version":"2.0.7723",
 "update_check_frequency":"5m","plugin_count":1419,
 "steam_branches":[{"name":"public","buildid":25353106}, …]}
```

⚠️ **uMod covers only 5 games now** — **TESTED:** rust 1419, hurtworld 80, reign-of-kings 62, 7-days-to-die 12, the-forest 1. Unturned/SevenDays legacy Oxide is gone. **uMod is effectively a Rust-only source.**

- **Oxide** — MIT (**TESTED** via GitHub licence API). Extract `Oxide.Rust-linux.zip` over `RustDedicated_Data/`. Plugins are `.cs` files dropped in **`oxide/plugins/`**; Oxide compiles and **hot-loads without restart**; `oxide.reload <name>` / `oxide.reload *`. Configs auto-generate in `oxide/config/`.
- **Carbon** — GPL-3.0 (**TESTED**). Release tag `production_build` with `Carbon.Linux.Release.tar.gz` (21 MB) / `.Minimal` variants. Extract at server root → `carbon/` + `HarmonyMods`. Plugins go in **`carbon/plugins/`**, configs in `carbon/configs/`, auto-load when `ScriptWatchers` is on. **Fully Oxide-plugin-compatible** — same `.cs` files.

Your installer needs a framework toggle (Oxide | Carbon) and writes to `oxide/plugins/` or `carbon/plugins/` accordingly. Same catalogue serves both.

**Paid Rust plugin marketplaces** (worth knowing, not catalogable): **Codefling** runs Invision Community's REST API — **TESTED:** `/api/core/hello` → `401 {"errorCode":"2S290/6","errorMessage":"NO_API_KEY"}`, key issued only by their admins. **Lone.Design** is WooCommerce behind a Cloudflare challenge (**TESTED:** `/wp-json/` → 403).

---

## 3. Steam Workshop — **the architecture finding that reshapes the project**

### (a) Metadata endpoints
**`POST https://api.steampowered.com/ISteamRemoteStorage/GetPublishedFileDetails/v1/` — NO KEY REQUIRED.** Independently **TESTED** twice. Form body `itemcount=N&publishedfileids[0]=…`. It's absent from partner docs but present in `ISteamWebAPIUtil/GetSupportedAPIList/v1/`.

Returns: `publishedfileid, result, creator, creator_app_id, consumer_app_id, filename, file_size, file_url, hcontent_file, preview_url, hcontent_preview, title, description (raw BBCode), time_created, time_updated, visibility, banned, ban_reason, subscriptions, favorited, lifetime_subscriptions, lifetime_favorited, views, tags[]`.

Not returned: vote data, short description, children, language. Those need `IPublishedFileService/*`. **Batches to at least 100 items/call (TESTED).** Per-item failures come back as `{"publishedfileid":"…","result":9}` while the envelope still says `result:1` — handle per-item.

🚨 **`file_url` is empty for every modern item.** **TESTED across all 11 target games:** GMod, ARK SE, PZ, Rust, Space Engineers, Barotrauma, KF2, Conan, Unturned → **all empty**. **Don't Starve Together is the sole exception** — it still uses the legacy path and returns a public CDN URL. **TESTED:** `curl https://cdn.steamusercontent.com/ugc/…` → 200, 32,910 bytes, valid zip, no account, no key. (Its tags also carry `all_clients_require_mod` — a free client/server flag.)

**`hcontent_file` cannot be converted to a URL.** **TESTED:** all three CDN host patterns 404. It's a SteamPipe manifest handle — steamcmd or `ISteamUGC::DownloadItem` only.

`IPublishedFileService/QueryFiles/v1` (the only search/discovery endpoint) **requires a key — TESTED: 403 keyless**; `GetDetails/v1` → **401**. Full param list captured: `query_type, page, cursor (use "*" first), numperpage, appid, creator_appid, requiredtags, excludedtags, match_all_tags, search_text, filetype, child_publishedfileid, days, language, totalonly, ids_only, return_vote_data, return_tags, return_kv_tags, return_previews, return_children, return_short_description, return_for_sale_data, return_metadata, return_playtime_stats`. **Page with `cursor`, not `page`.**

`ISteamRemoteStorage/GetCollectionDetails/v1/` — **no key, TESTED 200**. Returns only child IDs + sort order; hydrate via a second `GetPublishedFileDetails` call.

### (b) steamcmd — the anonymous question, answered properly
**Anonymous workshop download is a per-app developer opt-in**, not a global rule. Two hard sources:

1. [Barotrauma#7707](https://github.com/FakeFishGames/Barotrauma/issues/7707) — "Unable to use workshop_download_item with anonymous login in steamcmd", **still open**. Barotrauma (602960) does **not** support it.
2. A dev flipping the switch live in [GearCity's forum](https://steamcommunity.com/app/285110/discussions/0/686363730790031270/): *"Go to the 'Edit steamworks' setting. Click on the 'Workshop' tab. Find the setting titled **'Enable anonymous game servers to download workshop items'** and check the corresponding checkbox."* Dev replied *"Done. Enjoy."* — and it worked.

Valve's [implementation doc](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/workshop/implementation) acknowledges the case (*"If the user is not subscribed to the item (e.g. a Game Server using anonymous login), the workshop item will be downloaded and cached temporarily"*) but publishes no per-app list. **There is no way to know from outside — you must probe each appid in a sandbox.**

**The ownership rule** is documented only by the community and by hosts, never by Valve. Clearest statement, from the Pterodactyl Arma 3 egg:
> `STEAM_USER`: *"Account does not need to own Arma 3, but MUST BE a VALID Steam account (anonymous login cannot be used)."*
> `DISABLE_MOD_UPDATES`: *"**If the Steam account does not own the base Arma 3 game, Steam Workshop mod downloads/updates will not work.**"*

Note the asymmetry: server *binaries* need only a valid account; workshop *mods* need an **owning** account. [steam-for-linux#8028](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-for-linux/issues/8028) asks Valve directly and is **open with no reply**.

Files land at `steamapps/workshop/content/<appid>/<pubfileid>/`, state in `steamapps/workshop/appworkshop_<appid>.acf`.

### 🚨 (b2) The finding that changes your scope
**For 9 of your 11 games you never download anything.** You write an ID into a config file and the game server fetches it through Steam itself:

| Game | Mechanism | You download files? |
|---|---|---|
| Garry's Mod | `+host_workshop_collection <id>` **+ `-authkey <Web API key>`** | No |
| ARK: SE | `ActiveMods=` / `-mods=` | No |
| **ARK: ASA** | **CurseForge, not Workshop** | N/A |
| Project Zomboid | `WorkshopItems=` + `Mods=` | No |
| **Rust** | `server.levelurl "<direct .map URL>"` — **Workshop is skins-only** | N/A |
| Space Engineers | `<Mods>` in `sandbox_config.sbc` | No (owning account needed) |
| Barotrauma | anonymous **confirmed broken** | **Yes** |
| CS2 | `host_workshop_map` | No |
| Killing Floor 2 | `ServerSubscribedWorkshopItems` | No |
| Unturned | `Workshop_Download_IDs` | No |
| Don't Starve Together | `dedicated_server_mods_setup.lua` | No |
| Conan Exiles | `.pak` → `ConanSandbox/Mods` + `modlist.txt` | **Yes** |

Two corrections worth flagging upward: **ARK: Survival Ascended does not use Steam Workshop** (CurseForge), and **Rust Workshop is cosmetic skins, not maps** — indexing it would fill your catalogue with wallpaper and clothing.

Corroborating negative result: **LinuxGSM, the most-deployed open-source game-server manager, deliberately never touches the Workshop.** Its entire `mods_list.sh` sources from direct vendor URLs; zero references to `workshop`/`steamcmd`/`anonymous` in `mods_core.sh`. And of **216 Pterodactyl game eggs**, exactly **one** (Squad) calls `workshop_download_item` — **none of your eleven**.

### (c) Legal — quotes
**[Steam Subscriber Agreement](https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/)**

§2.A: *"Valve hereby grants… the right, to use the Content and Services **for your personal, non-commercial use**… The Content and Services are licensed, not sold."*

§2.G: *"you may not, in whole or in part, copy, photocopy, reproduce, publish, **distribute**… the Content and Services… without the prior consent, in writing, of Valve."* and *"you are not entitled to: … (ii) **host or provide matchmaking services for the Content and Services**… **for any purpose including… as part of content aggregation networks, websites or services, without the prior written consent of Valve**; or (iii) exploit the Content and Services or any of its parts for any commercial purpose."*

§2.E (the counterweight): *"you may use the Valve Dedicated Server Software on an **unlimited number of computers** for the purpose of hosting online multiplayer games of Valve products."* — §2.G forbids hosting without consent, §2.E grants it, **but only for Valve's own dedicated-server software** (CS2, GMod's Source base). Third-party games are governed by their publishers' EULAs.

§1.C: *"you must not use your Account to enable a violation of this Agreement by others, such as through **their commercial use of Steam Content and Services**."* — aims squarely at the one-company-account-serving-many-customers model.

§6.A: *"you grant **Valve and its affiliates** the worldwide, non-exclusive right to use, reproduce, modify… your User Generated Content… for the purpose of the operation… of the Steam service."* — **the grant runs to Valve, not to hosts**; sublicensing is only referenced as *"any sub-license granted by Valve"*.

§6.B: *"any **Subscriber** receiving distribution of your Workshop Contribution will have the same rights… as are set out in this Agreement for any other Subscriptions"* and *"Specific Workshop-Enabled Apps… may contain special terms ('App-Specific Terms')."* **Your customer, as a Subscriber, has a personal non-commercial licence. You, as a business handing them the file, do not obviously have one.**

🚨 **The standalone Steam Workshop Legal Agreement no longer exists.** **TESTED:** `steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/workshoplegalagreement` returns 200 with one line — *"Click here to view the latest Steam Subscriber Agreement."* Any guidance citing it as a separate document is citing a dead page.

**[Steam Web API Terms of Use](https://steamcommunity.com/dev/apiterms)** (last updated July 2010):
> "you may access the Steam Web API… and distribute Steam Data to end users **for their personal use** via your Application"
> "**You will only retrieve Steam Data about a Steam end user as requested by the end user.**"
> "**You agree to keep your Steam Web API key confidential, and not to share it with any third party. This license is personal to you and specific to your Application.**"
> "**You are limited to one hundred thousand (100,000) calls to the Steam Web API per day.**"
> §13: *"You may not transfer, assign, or delegate the API Terms of Use and your Steam Web API key to any third party."*

🚨 **Direct collision:** the Garry's Mod install path requires `-authkey <Steam Web API key>` **on the game server**. Putting Nxeon's key on customer GMod boxes is arguably sharing/delegating it. **Have each customer supply their own key** — that's the defensible design.

**Caching workshop metadata is not addressed anywhere.** The nearest clause ("only… as requested by the end user") is written about *user* data and fits poorly, but points away from speculative bulk pre-indexing. **Genuinely ambiguous — don't assume a catalogue is permitted.**

### (e) What hosts actually do
The pattern is uniform: **nobody redistributes Workshop files; they write IDs into config.**
- **Apex Hosting** ships the closest thing to what you're building — a Workshop search panel that *"automatically adds the mod IDs to the config file."* A metadata search + config writer, **not a file mirror**.
- **Nitrado** ships a **CurseForge** browser on the dashboard but **no Steam Workshop file browser** — that looks deliberate.
- **Host Havoc, Shockbyte, PingPerfect, DatHost** — all ID-into-config.
- **GTXGaming** says the quiet part out loud for Space Engineers: *"This requires a user and password of a Steam account which **owns** the Space Engineers game to get mods."*

**No host claims Valve permission; no Valve statement about hosting providers exists at all.** Everyone operates in the silence.

**Risk gradient:** ID-into-config (lowest, and it covers 9/11 games) → steamcmd under a company account (you're now reproducing and distributing commercially, squarely inside §2.G) → mirroring files or re-serving those public DST CDN objects (highest; trivial technically, worst legally).

---

## 4. Minecraft beyond Modrinth

### PaperMC Hangar — **Tier 1, build on this**
`https://hangar.papermc.io/api/v1/`, OpenAPI at **`/v3/api-docs`** (183 KB). **3,833 projects** — small, curated, and **free by policy**: their guidelines state *"Functionality may not be hidden behind a paywall or an author-granted license key."* No premium logic needed.

**Licence is a first-class field:** `settings.license = {name, url, type}`. Census of the top 50 by downloads: **43/50 (86%) carry a real type** — GPL 23, MIT 11, AGPL 2, LGPL 3, Apache 1, Other 3, Unspecified 7.

Per-version payload gives `fileInfo.sha256Hash`, `sizeBytes`, per-platform `downloadUrl`, **and `pluginDependencies`** — everything an installer needs. Anonymous download verified byte-for-byte against the advertised hash. ⚠️ **Sending `Accept: application/java-archive` returns 406** — send nothing or `*/*`.

Rate limit, quoted from their own spec: *"**The default rate limit is set at 20 requests every 5 seconds** with an initial overdraft for extra leniency… **If applicable, always cache responses.**"* and *"Please also set a meaningful `User-Agent` header."* Anonymous and authenticated get the same throughput.

Two endpoints to design around: **`GET /api/v1/versions/hash/{sha256}`** (reverse-lookup a jar — identify customer-uploaded plugins, detect stale or tampered installs; **nobody else offers this**) and `GET /api/v1/platforms/{platform}/versions` (authoritative MC compat matrix). *"all routes not listed here should be considered internal… Do not use them."*

[Hangar Terms](https://hangar.papermc.io/terms) contain **no clauses at all** on API use, scraping, caching, or commercial use. Their content licence is scoped *"on and through the Service"* — **your redistribution right comes from `settings.license`**, which is exactly why that field matters.

### 🚨 PaperMC server jars — your v2 knowledge is stale
```
GET https://api.papermc.io/v2/projects/paper
{"ok":false,"error":"sunset","message":"This API version has been sunset…"}
```
Same for velocity, waterfall, folia. **The live API is `https://fill.papermc.io/v3/`** — `/v3/projects`, `/v3/projects/paper/versions/{v}/builds/latest` returning `downloads["server:default"]` with `checksums.sha256`, `size`, `url`. Builds carry a `channel` (`ALPHA`/`STABLE`) — **filter on it before auto-updating customers.**

Mandatory, from their [downloads-service docs](https://docs.papermc.io/misc/downloads-service/): *"All requests must now include a valid User-Agent header that: Clearly identifies your software or company; **Is not generic (e.g. curl, wget…)**; Includes a contact URL or email address."* Use `Nxeon-NxLabs/1.0 (https://nxeon.cloud)`. Also: *"**We emphatically do not recommend using unstable builds or auto-updaters within production environments.**"*

### 🚨 SpigotMC — do not ship Spiget-backed installs
**SpigotMC does have two semi-official APIs**, contrary to the brief. `api.spigotmc.org/simple/0.2/index.php?action=…` — actions discovered by sending a bogus one: `listResources, getResource, getResourcesByAuthor, listResourceCategories, getResourceUpdate, getResourceUpdates, getAuthor, findAuthor`. Returns `premium.price`/`premium.currency` and `external_download_url` directly. Plus `api.spigotmc.org/legacy/update.php?resource=<id>` → bare version string. Neither offers downloads; neither is documented. Both live on hosts *not* behind the Cloudflare challenge that guards `www.spigotmc.org`.

**Spiget** (`api.spiget.org/v2`, unofficial): 90,422 resources, 119,130 authors. Pagination via `x-page-*` headers. **No licence field anywhere** — grepped the swagger and censused live responses; zero. Three fatal problems:
1. **`external:true` resources return an HTML web page, not a jar.** EssentialsX's `/download` lands on the GitHub *release tag page*. An installer following it blindly writes HTML into `plugins/`. Spiget's own spec: *"The `external` field of a resource should be checked before downloading, to not receive any unexpected data."*
2. **Premium → 404.** Spiget doesn't mirror paid jars.
3. **Version pinning is broken.** `/versions/{id}/download` redirects to spigotmc.org and dies on Cloudflare (`cf-mitigated: challenge`). **Spiget can only reliably serve each plugin's single latest jar.** For a host where "pin the version matching the customer's MC version" is table stakes, that alone disqualifies it.

And the legal position is bad. [SpigotMC ToS](https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/spigot-terms/) §4: *"**You may not copy, distribute or disclose any part of the Platform in any medium, including without limitation by any automated or non-automated 'scraping'**"* and *"**You may not use any robot, spider, crawler, scraper or other automated means or interface not provided by us** to access the Platform or to extract data."* [Forum rules](https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/spigot-rules/): *"**Do not access the forums via automated mechanisms**"* and *"Do not distribute 'Premium Resources' to those who have not purchased them."*

Spiget is exactly the "interface not provided by us" the ToS names — and the SpiGetOrg repo list includes **`spiget-puppeteer-client`**, i.e. it drives a headless browser to defeat Cloudflare. Single maintainer, hobby-funded.

**Recommendation: use `simple/0.2` for discovery metadata only, then resolve to GitHub Releases via `sourceCodeLink` and install from there.** That converts a shaky path into a clean one.

### 🎁 Bukkit ServerMods API — the surprise winner
`api.curseforge.com/servermods/` is **alive, current, and needs no API key**:
```
GET /servermods/projects?search=vault      → [{"id":33184,"name":"Vault","slug":"vault",…}]
GET /servermods/files?projectIds=31043     → 97 files, newest worldedit-bukkit-7.4.5.jar,
                                              gameVersion 26.2, released 2026-06-16
                                              downloadUrl https://files.forgecdn.net/files/8607/421/…
```
That CDN URL serves a real 7.7 MB jar unauthenticated. Fields: `dateReleased, downloadUrl, fileName, fileUrl, gameVersion, md5, name, projectId, releaseType`. 15 rapid requests → all 200. **Undocumented, unversioned, no licence field, BukkitDev-era coverage only** (`search=luckperms` finds nothing modern). **Free long-tail upside with a fallback — not a foundation.**

`dev.bukkit.org` is confirmed a skinned CurseForge front-end.

### 🚫 Planet Minecraft — exclude entirely
No API. [Terms of Use](https://www.planetminecraft.com/terms_of_use/), *"you agree that you shall not:"*
> "**5:** … otherwise systematically extract data or data fields"
> "**6:** Sell access to or the use of this website, including any content contained on, downloaded or accessed from this website"
> "**7:** Redistribute any content, including data, provided by us in any manner whatsoever"
> "**8:** Intentionally alter the format in which site data is provided by us or otherwise circumvent our regular interfaces to such data"
> "**9:** Embed or import any site data provided by us into any information services…, data files or application software"

Five clauses, each independently fatal. They run an active DMCA programme with a named agent. Don't route around it with a "paste a URL" flow either — clause 9 covers that.

## 5. CurseForge — **usable, but two contract clauses are real blockers**

### (a)–(b) API
Base `https://api.curseforge.com`, header **`x-api-key`**. Keys are **approval-gated** via console.curseforge.com; the [support article](https://support.curseforge.com/support/solutions/articles/9000208346) describes a reviewed application and says the team assesses *"How it impacts on Authors' earnings / How it affects CurseForge's servers and CDN / **How it takes Authors' consent** when it comes to third party distribution."* Keys are **game-scoped** (`/v1/games` = *"all games that are available to the provided API key"*).

Three corrections to your endpoint list: **there is no `GET /v1/fingerprints`** (POST-only), and the Minecraft helpers are **singular** — `/v1/minecraft/version` and `/v1/minecraft/modloader`. Everything else confirmed, plus `POST /v1/mods` (bulk, same game only), `POST /v1/mods/files`, `/v1/mods/{id}/description`, `/v1/mods/{id}/files/{fid}/changelog`.

**Hard pagination wall**, verbatim: *"The maximum page size is 50 results per page and capped at 10000 total results. Note: The limit is (index + pageSize <= 10,000)."* You must shard by category/version/loader to enumerate anything large.

### (c) Fields — **no licence, confirmed**
Full `Mod` schema captured (`id, gameId, name, slug, links{websiteUrl,wikiUrl,issuesUrl,sourceUrl}, summary, status, downloadCount, categories[], classId, authors[], logo{thumbnailUrl,url}, screenshots[], latestFiles[], allowModDistribution, isAvailable, thumbsUpCount, dateModified…`).

**The word "license" appears 4 times in the entire 211 KB docs page — all in legal boilerplate, zero in any schema.** Corroborated: cfwidget.com returns `"license": ""` for JEI, JourneyMap, AE2, Create. Licence lives only on the website's author-editable License tab — and scraping `curseforge.com` is expressly prohibited *and* Cloudflare-blocked from this box.

For a hosting installer the two most valuable `File` fields are **`isServerPack` / `serverPackFileId`** — many modpacks ship a distinct server-side pack.

### (d) `allowModDistribution`
> "If you turn this option off **Any 3rd-party service, website or client will not have access to your projects or files via the 3rd-party API.**"
> "**We recommend choosing a license preference that is compatible with your distribution choice. In any case - the API will respect the toggle choice over the license type choice.**"

Internalise that last sentence: **an MIT-licensed mod can still be `allowModDistribution=false`, and CurseForge enforces the toggle over the licence.** When false, `downloadUrl` is `null`.

No official prevalence figure exists. Anecdotes: All the Mods 9 (~400 mods) → 3 blocked; a 114-mod pack → 4 blocked. It clusters on popular libraries, so **a ~1–3% per-mod rate becomes a ~50% per-modpack failure rate.** Every serious tool gives up and hands it to a human — `itzg/docker-minecraft-server` (your closest analogue): *"For mod, modpacks, and world files that are not allowed for automated download, the container path `/downloads` can be attached and matching files will be retrieved from there."*

**Design implication:** persist and refresh the flag, badge or hide blocked mods **in the catalogue UI** rather than failing at install, and ship the SFTP/upload fallback in v1.

### (e) 🔧 Your 403 — diagnosed, with a live reproduction
I reproduced both surfaces independently.

**`api.curseforge.com`** — **TESTED:** no key → `403`, `content-length: 0`, `x-cache: Error from cloudfront`. Bogus key → identical. Adding a descriptive User-Agent and `Accept: application/json` → identical. **CloudFront rejects the key at the edge before the app sees it.**

**Triage rule:** *empty body ⇒ auth problem. HTML body (`"ERROR: The request could not be satisfied… Request blocked"`) ⇒ rate limit.* That's your fastest diagnostic — there are no rate-limit headers at all.

**Most likely cause of your specific 403: shell/Compose `$`-expansion eating the key.** CurseForge keys are bcrypt-shaped (`$2a$10$…`); `$2a` and `$10` get silently expanded away in `.env` files and Docker Compose, truncating the key. This is the single most-reported cause ([itzg#3591](https://github.com/itzg/docker-minecraft-server/issues/3591)). **Check the key's exact byte length at the point of use.** Second possibility: the key isn't authorised for the game you're querying.

**Ruled out — TESTED:**
- **Not a Cloudflare datacenter-IP block.** `api.curseforge.com` and forgecdn are **AWS CloudFront + Fastly/ioRiver/S3, not Cloudflare**. `media.forgecdn.net` (icons) returns **200 from this box**. (`www.curseforge.com` — the *website* — *is* Cloudflare and *does* challenge this IP; separate surface.)
- **Not a User-Agent requirement.** Jars fetched with empty, default-curl, and browser UAs → all 200.

**The CDN path rule** (I initially got 403s from guessed paths, which is exactly the trap):
```
https://mediafilez.forgecdn.net/files/{fileId // 1000}/{fileId % 1000}/{fileName}
```
⚠️ **The second segment is NOT zero-padded.** fileId `8851009` → `8851/9` ✅ 200; `8851/009` ❌ 403. The S3 bucket denies listing, so **a missing key returns 403 `<Error><Code>AccessDenied</Code>`, not 404** — which is why a wrong path looks identical to a permissions failure. That is almost certainly what a hand-built URL was hitting.

### 🚨 Time-sensitive
[CurseForge blog, Jun 10 2026](https://blog.curseforge.com/introducing-api-key-authentication-for-curseforge-file-downloads/): *"We're rolling out API key authentication for direct file downloads from the CurseForge CDN… This is aimed at… **launchers, modpack installers, server tools**… **Phase: Future (July 16th) — API key required. Requests without a valid key return 401 Unauthorized.**"* **Observed today, two months past that date: not yet enforced** (unauthenticated CDN downloads still 200). **Build `x-api-key` into the CDN fetch path now** — the failure mode is a hard 401 on every install.

### (g) 🚨 The two contract clauses that should change your architecture
[CurseForge 3rd Party API Terms](https://support.curseforge.com/support/solutions/articles/9000207405) — *"THIS IS A BINDING CONTRACT"*, governed by Israeli law:

> "Developer shall not… (e) **save or cache any data obtained through the API or SDK.** In addition, Developer shall not use the API or SDK… in order build any product or service that **competes, directly or indirectly, with CF, CurseForge for Studios, or the Platform.**"

**A literal reading of "save or cache any data obtained through the API" forbids the NxLabs catalogue outright.** You cannot engineer around this — it needs written clarification as part of the key application. And a hosting company shipping a mod browser is at least arguable as an indirect competitor. Termination is 14 days' notice for material breach.

Also: the key is *"non-transferable and may not be shared with any third party"*, VPN/proxy access is prohibited, and above an undisclosed quota *"continued use… may require Developer to enter into a written licensing agreement… which may contain payment requirements."*

[Overwolf Platforms ToU](https://legal.overwolf.com/docs/overwolf/platform/platform-terms-of-use/) §3.3 grants a licence *"**for non-commercial purposes**"*; §7.2(iv) forbids *"any robot, spider, crawler, scraper, or other automated means"* against the website; §7.2(viii) requires *"prior written consent"* to use their marks — so the CurseForge logo in your UI needs sign-off.

### (f) Rate limits
**Nothing documented, no headers.** Throttling surfaces as CloudFront 403-with-HTML-body. itzg's advice: *"remove the `restart` policy parameter until you have your container setup initially. Otherwise, you will exceed the rate limit."* — a single crash-loop trips it. Reset window reported as ~1 hour. **Implement your own token bucket; catalogue sync must be a sharded, resumable background job, never on a request path.**

## 6. The long tail

### ⭐ Satisfactory — ficsit.app: best-in-class for a host
`POST https://api.ficsit.app/v2/query` — GraphQL, **no auth**, **introspection fully open**. **I verified independently:** `getMods` → `count: 1567`.

The two killer fields, **TESTED**:
```json
"versions":[{"version":"2026.3.28","required_on_remote":true,
  "targets":[{"targetName":"LinuxServer","link":"/v1/version/…/LinuxServer/download","size":40384686,"hash":"664153ba…"},
             {"targetName":"Windows","size":237473374,…},{"targetName":"WindowsServer",…}]}]
```
⚠️ **Correction: `required_on_remote` lives on `Version`, not `Mod`** (I hit `Cannot query field "required_on_remote" on type "Mod"`). It tells you outright whether the mod must go on the server, and `targets` gives you a **LinuxServer build at 40 MB vs 237 MB for the client**. Download is a 302 to Backblaze B2, unauthenticated, and the SHA-256 matched the API's `hash` exactly.

**No licence field** — I introspected all 93 types for `licen|legal|copyright|terms`: **zero hits**. Confirmed independently by dumping `Mod`'s full field list. `source_url` is your only proxy.

Server install: SML 3.7.0+; [ficsit-cli](https://github.com/satisfactorymodding/ficsit-cli) *"can be installed locally or directly on the server itself"*; connects over SFTP/FTP/SMB/local path pointed at the dir containing `FactoryServer.sh`; **the server must be shut down** before installing. You can skip ficsit-cli entirely and just fetch the LinuxServer target — but then you own dependency resolution via `versions.dependencies`.

⚠️ **ToS unverified** — `ficsit.app/tos` is a client-rendered SPA and the forums mirror 503'd. Search-surfaced (unconfirmed) text includes *"You are not entitled to redistribute, repackage, sell, or otherwise distribute content without express permission."* **Have someone open it in a browser before finalising the caching policy.**

### ⭐ Vintage Story — official, documented, friendly terms
`https://mods.vintagestory.at/api/` — plain GET, no auth. **I verified independently:** `/api/mod/primitivesurvival` → 200, 98 KB; `/api/mods` → 8,600 mods; `/api/gameversions`, `/api/tags`, `/api/authors` all 200.

**Two free fields you'd otherwise have to infer: `side` (`"both"|"server"|"client"`) and `type`.** `side` is exactly the server-side filter you want.

**No licence field** (confirmed by key dump). `sourcecodeurl` is the proxy. Download **TESTED unauthenticated: 200, 2.27 MB zip**, via `?fileid=`, `/download/{fileid}/{filename}`, or the `mainfile` CDN URL directly.

Bonus: an undocumented v2 built for exactly this — `GET /api/v2/mods/install-information?ids=<modidstr>@<version>` (GET only; POST 405s) and `/api/v2/mods/{modid}/releases/latest`. Use those for update checks instead of re-pulling the 3.8 MB dump.

[Terms](https://mods.vintagestory.at/terms) — the most favourable in the report:
> "**Mod User:** A visitor of this site that downloads your mod **or a player that downloads your mod through the game client**."
> "Note that **no license does not imply public domain, but that all rights are reserved.** … you are not allowed to reupload, modified or not, any such mods without explicit approval."

Fetching on a customer's behalf is fine; **standing up a mirror is a "reupload."**

### mod.io — strategically important, but gated
`https://api.mod.io/v1`, **auth mandatory** (**TESTED:** 401 without a key). Rate limits: **game-linked key = unlimited; user-linked key = 60/min**; OAuth 120/min; per-IP 1,000/min. **As a host you get the 60/min tier** — build incremental sync on `date_updated`.

**No licence field** (`metadata_blob` is free-form). Downloads are **time-limited signed URLs** (`binary_url` + `date_expires`) with MD5 `filehash`.

[Terms](https://mod.io/legal/terms) are the most third-party-friendly anywhere here: *"User Generated Content is publicly available information which is shared with other users, other third parties, and **is made available through the mod.io API**."* Their [AUP](https://mod.io/legal/aup) contains **no anti-scraping, anti-automation, or anti-caching clause at all**. And they run a **Reseller / Enhanced License Rights** framework under [mod.io/monetization](https://mod.io/monetization) — **the only sanctioned commercial-resale route in this entire report.** They sell "mod.io for Studios" and are commercially motivated to talk to hosts.

⚠️ **But:** [docs.mod.io/multiplayer/dedicated-servers](https://docs.mod.io/multiplayer/dedicated-servers) says, verbatim: *"**We are currently building out the Dedicated Servers feature.** Reach out to developers@mod.io to learn more."* **Not GA.** Known users include Baldur's Gate 3 and MORDHAU; the full game list needs a key (`GET /v1/games?_limit=100` — highest-value 10 minutes of follow-up from this whole report).

### 🚫 Nexus Mods — **no. Four independent disqualifiers, each fatal**
1. **Your installer is a named prohibited use.** [AUP](https://help.nexusmods.com/article/114-api-acceptable-use-policy): *"**Storing user API keys on your own server and/or using them without the action being initiated by the user.**"*
2. **Your catalogue is a named prohibited use.** *"**Fetching data en-masse with the intent to rehost this information on your own service (i.e. scraping).**"* Reinforced by ToS §11: *"You shall not conduct, facilitate, authorise or permit any text or data mining or web scraping… for any purpose."*
3. **Commercial use needs a licence you don't have.** ToS §10: *"**You must not use any part of the content on our site for commercial purposes without obtaining a licence**"*; downloads are *"for your own personal use"* only.
4. **The download mechanism is engineered to prevent it.** v1 spec, verbatim: *"Non-premium members must provide the key and expiry from the .nxm link provided by the website… **This ensures that all non-premium members must access the website to download through the API.**"* Error: *`403: "You don't have permission to get download links from the API without visting nexusmods.com - this is for premium users only."`*

Plus: rate limits are **per-USER, not per-application** — *"refreshing your API key… will not allow you to exceed the rate limits."* Your traffic burns your customer's quota and locks them out of Vortex. (Figures also disagree between sources: the spec says 2,500/day → 100/hr; the [help article, updated Jun 3 2026](https://help.nexusmods.com/article/105) says **20,000/day → 500/hr**. Take the newer one.)

Two structural corrections: **`app.nexusmods.com` no longer resolves** — current docs are [api-docs.nexusmods.com](https://api-docs.nexusmods.com/), which documents **v3** (author/upload-oriented, no consumer download endpoint). And **v1 has no browse or search endpoint at all** — only `latest_added`/`latest_updated`/`trending`, **10 items each**. You couldn't enumerate the catalogue even if it were permitted.

There *is* an undocumented **`POST https://api.nexusmods.com/v2/graphql` that works with no key at all**, with open introspection and a `mods(filter:…)` query — technically the most capable option available and the most legally exposed. Don't.

**Only defensible design: deep-link out to the mod page (ToS §27 permits linking), customer downloads under their own account, clean SFTP/upload path in.**

### GitHub Releases — the licence oracle
`/repos/{o}/{r}/releases/latest`, and **`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/license` returns a real `spdx_id`** — **TESTED**: OxideMod → `MIT`, Carbon → `GPL-3.0`.

⚠️ `browser_download_url` **redirects to a signed URL expiring in ~1 hour** — the browser URL is stable and cacheable, **the resolved one is not; never persist it.** `GET /licenses` returns only 13 featured licences — pass `?featured=false`. `"spdx_id": "NOASSERTION"` means unknown, **not permissive**.

**Rate limits, TESTED live** (I exhausted them mid-research: `x-ratelimit-limit: 60, remaining: 0`): unauth **60/hr**; PAT **5,000/hr**; ⚠️ **correction — GitHub App on an org is 5,000 + 50/user, capped at 12,500, not 15,000; the 15,000 figure is Enterprise Cloud only.** Asset downloads don't consume the REST limit.

[ToS](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service) §D.5: *"you grant other Users a nonexclusive, worldwide license to use, display, perform and reproduce (by forking) Your Content **through the Service**."* That grant is scoped to GitHub itself. **Your right to install comes solely from the repo's licence — if `/license` is null or NOASSERTION, treat it as all-rights-reserved: hot-link only.**

## Cross-cutting conclusions

**1. Licence metadata barely exists.** Only **Hangar** (86% populated), **Factorio** (100%, non-SPDX), **uMod** (85%, slugs), **Modrinth** (real SPDX — `{"id":"Apache-2.0",…}`) and **GitHub** (real SPDX) expose one. CurseForge, Steam, ficsit, Vintage Story, mod.io, Spiget, Polymart, ServerMods all have **nothing**. Build a normalisation table keyed on each source's stable id (not display title), fall back to GitHub `/license` whenever `source_url`/`sourcecodeurl` points there, and design the UI for *"License: not provided by source."* SPDX 3.29.0 (740 ids) covers every observed value — MIT, GPL-3.0-*, LGPL-3.0-*, Apache-2.0, Unlicense, MPL-2.0, WTFPL, ISC, BSD-3-Clause, CC-BY-*, CC0-1.0 all map cleanly.

**2. Every single source converges on the same posture: fetch-on-behalf-of-user, never mirror.** Vintage Story says it outright. Factorio's top-two custom licences forbid commercial use but permit unmodified redistribution with attribution. Steam's grant runs to Valve. mod.io's runs to mod.io and the publisher. GitHub's is scoped "through the Service." CurseForge forbids caching entirely. **Architect the installer as a just-in-time proxy — stream origin → customer server at install time, short-lived local cache at most.** That one decision keeps you clean across all of them simultaneously, and it also means the expiring signed URLs (GitHub, mod.io) were never a problem.

**3. Build tiers:**
- **Tier 1, build now:** Hangar (+ Fill v3 for server jars — **your existing v2 integration is sunset and returning errors**), uMod/Oxide+Carbon, Factorio, ficsit.app, Vintage Story, Bukkit ServerMods, GitHub Releases.
- **Tier 1, trivially easy:** ARK: ASA — write `-mods=`, restart, done.
- **Tier 2, gated:** CurseForge (apply for the key; **get the cache and competitor clauses resolved in writing first**), mod.io (get a key, run `/games`, ask about the Reseller framework).
- **Tier 3, ID-into-config only:** Steam Workshop for the 9 games that self-fetch. Metadata catalogue via the keyless `GetPublishedFileDetails`; `QueryFiles` search needs a key and a 100k/day budget. **Require customers to supply their own Web API key for Garry's Mod.**
- **Tier 4, download-and-place (only two games):** Barotrauma (anonymous confirmed broken) and Conan Exiles.
- **Excluded:** Nexus Mods (link-out only), Planet Minecraft, Spiget-backed installs.

**4. Build the "download → parse internal manifest → write config" pipeline once.** Project Zomboid (`mod.info` → `Mods=`), tModLoader (`.tmod` → `enabled.json`), and Palworld (`Info.json` → `IsServer`) all need exactly that shape, and none of the three internal IDs are available from Workshop metadata.

**5. Immediate action items:** (a) check your CurseForge key's byte length at the point of use — bcrypt `$`-expansion is the most likely cause of your 403, and use the `divmod(fileId, 1000)` un-padded CDN rule; (b) migrate PaperMC off the sunset v2 API to `fill.papermc.io/v3` with an identifying User-Agent; (c) get a mod.io key and run one `/games` call.
